## P4 - Drop unnecessary `slices.Clone` before `slices.DeleteFunc` in `deployFn`

**Location:** [cmd/deploy.go:336-343](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fa1070982d24f060198ba82bebd9dd74d4048e33/cmd/deploy.go#L336-L343)

**Problem:** The PR moved the internal-container filter out of `PrintContainerInspect` into `deployFn` and wrapped it with `slices.Clone(result.Containers)`. The clone exists to shield `result.Containers` from `slices.DeleteFunc` mutation, but `result.Containers` is never read again&#58; `deployFn` returns immediately after the `PrintContainerInspect(containers, o)` call on line 343, and the other consumers of `result` use different fields.

**Trigger:** Every `deploy` or `redeploy` invocation that prints the container summary.

**Impact:** One avoidable slice copy per `deploy` &#40;negligible at realistic lab sizes&#41; and a maintenance question&#58; readers may assume `result.Containers` is needed unfiltered elsewhere when it is not.

**Suggested correction:** Apply `slices.DeleteFunc` directly to `result.Containers` instead of cloning it, for example `containers := slices.DeleteFunc(result.Containers, func(ctr clabruntime.GenericContainer) bool { return ctr.Labels[clabconstants.InternalNode] == "true" })`. If a defensive copy is intentionally preferred, add a brief comment naming the protected caller. Optional change; either form is acceptable.


## Coverage

- Source-only review of all 15 changed paths across head &#40;fa1070982d24f060198ba82bebd9dd74d4048e33&#41; and base &#40;58ef6910e7165169cff3725c29529b635e635e59&#41;; no tests, builds, or benchmarks were executed, so runtime claims rest on code reading.
- Traced `logicalNodeContainers` pass logic, label semantics &#40;`ToolType`, `InternalNode`, `RootNodeName`, `NodeName`&#41;, the `-t` label-list plus node-forge merge and dedup, tool labeling via `createLabelsMap`, and sros/srl `GetContainers` CPM-A/holder fallback semantics.
- Verified the Clabernetes path bypasses `logicalNodeContainers` by construction&#58; `ListLabRuntimeContainers` emits one entry per topology node state with no `InternalNode`/`ToolType` labels, so removing the filter from `PrintContainerInspect` does not regress c9s inspect output.
- Confirmed CPM slots are mandatory for distributed SR-SIM&#58; `deployFabric` calls `cpmSlot()`, which errors when neither slot A nor B exists, so inspect cannot encounter a deployed lab whose distributed node has no CPM container; `calcComponentName`/`renameDone` guarantee component names are always `<root>-<slot>` at creation time, matching the inspect heuristic.
- Checked remaining `PrintContainerInspect` callers &#40;[`cmd/inspect.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fa1070982d24f060198ba82bebd9dd74d4048e33/cmd/inspect.go#L1-L1), [`cmd/deploy.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fa1070982d24f060198ba82bebd9dd74d4048e33/cmd/deploy.go#L1-L1), [`cmd/labruntime_gaps_test.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fa1070982d24f060198ba82bebd9dd74d4048e33/cmd/labruntime_gaps_test.go#L1-L1)&#41;; test fixtures lack internal labels, so their output is unchanged by the filter relocation.
- Verified test plumbing by inspection&#58; `Run Checked Pipeline` now lives in [`tests/common.robot`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fa1070982d24f060198ba82bebd9dd74d4048e33/tests/common.robot#L1-L1) with `RETURN` of rc/stdout and is imported by [`09-srsim-pause-container.robot`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fa1070982d24f060198ba82bebd9dd74d4048e33/tests/13-srsim/09-srsim-pause-container.robot#L1-L1); `Deploy SR-SIM Lab`, `Destroy SR-SIM Lab`, and `Check SR-SIM License` exist in [`tests/srsim.robot`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fa1070982d24f060198ba82bebd9dd74d4048e33/tests/srsim.robot#L1-L1); CI matrix additions &#40;`05*.robot` in [`srlinux-tests.yml`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fa1070982d24f060198ba82bebd9dd74d4048e33/.github/workflows/srlinux-tests.yml#L1-L1), [`15-inspect-views.robot`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fa1070982d24f060198ba82bebd9dd74d4048e33/tests/13-srsim/15-inspect-views.robot#L1-L1) in the srsim components shard&#41; match only the new suite files.
- Intentional, documented behavior changes are noted but not filed as defects&#58; the default inspect view hides tool containers &#40;`sshx`, `gotty`, `api-server`&#41; and netns holders unless `--containers`/`--details` is given, and with `-t` even `--containers` excludes tools because their `NodeName` is not a topology node, matching the documented &#39;`-t` lists only containers of nodes defined in the topology file&#39; semantics.
- No schema-domain change was introduced &#40;no [`clab.schema.json`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fa1070982d24f060198ba82bebd9dd74d4048e33/schemas/clab.schema.json#L1-L1) properties added or removed&#41;, so no schema comparison was required.
- The O&#40;n^2&#41; `Contains`-based dedup in the `-t` merge is bounded by per-lab container counts and reuses existing runtime list helpers; it was not raised as a finding under the repository&#39;s performance ceilings.

1: ---

5: 
6: # Karpathy behavioral guidelines
7: 
8: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Merge with project-specific instructions as needed.
9: 
10: **Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.
11: 
12: ## 1. Think Before Coding
13: 
14: **Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**
15: 
16: Before implementing:
17: 
18: - State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
19: - If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
20: - If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
21: - If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.
22: 
23: ## 2. Simplicity First
24: 
25: **Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**
26: 
27: - No features beyond what was asked.
28: - No abstractions for single-use code.
29: - No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
30: - No error handling for impossible scenarios.
31: - If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.
32: 
33: Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.
34: 
35: ## 3. Surgical Changes
36: 
37: **Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**
38: 
39: When editing existing code:
40: 
41: - Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
42: - Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
43: - Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
44: - If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.
45: 
46: When your changes create orphans:
47: 
48: - Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
49: - Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.
50: 
51: The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.
52: 
53: ## 4. Goal-Driven Execution
54: 
55: **Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**
56: 
57: Transform tasks into verifiable goals:
58: 
59: - "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
60: - "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
61: - "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"
62: 
63: For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:
64: 
65: ```
66: 1. [Step] → verify: [check]
67: 2. [Step] → verify: [check]
68: 3. [Step] → verify: [check]
69: ```
70: 
71: Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: **These guidelines are working if:** fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.

(End of file - total 75 lines)

Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**\n\nBefore implementing:\n\n- State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.\n- If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.\n- If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.\n- If something is unclear, stop. 1: ---
2: description: Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode. Always pick the simplest solution that works.
3: globs:
4: alwaysApply: true
5: ---
6: 
7: # Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode
8: 
9: You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. The best code is the code never written.
10: 
11: Before writing any code, stop at the first rung that holds:
12: 
13: 1. Does this need to be built at all? (YAGNI)
14: 2. Does it already exist in this codebase? Reuse the helper, util, or pattern that's already here, don't re-write it.
15: 3. Does the standard library already do this? Use it.
16: 4. Does a native platform feature cover it? Use it.
17: 5. Does an already-installed dependency solve it? Use it.
18: 6. Can this be one line? Make it one line.
19: 7. Only then: write the minimum code that works.
20: 
21: The ladder runs after you understand the problem, not instead of it: read the task and the code it touches, trace the real flow end to end, then climb.
22: 
23: Bug fix = root cause, not symptom: a report names a symptom. Grep every caller of the function you touch and fix the shared function once — one guard there is a smaller diff than one per caller, and patching only the path the ticket names leaves a sibling caller still broken.
24: 
25: Rules:
26: 
27: - No abstractions that weren't explicitly requested.
28: - No new dependency if it can be avoided.
29: - No boilerplate nobody asked for.
30: - Deletion over addition. Boring over clever. Fewest files possible.
31: - Shortest working diff wins, but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
32: - Question complex requests: "Do you actually need X, or does Y cover it?"
33: - Pick the edge-case-correct option when two stdlib approaches are the same size, lazy means less code, not the flimsier algorithm.
34: - Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path.
35: 
36: Not lazy about: understanding the problem (read it fully and trace the real flow before picking a rung, a small diff you don't understand is just laziness dressed up as efficiency), input validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, the calibration real hardware needs (the platform is never the spec ideal, a clock drifts, a sensor reads off), anything explicitly requested. Lazy code without its check is unfinished: non-trivial logic leaves ONE runnable check behind, the smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks (an assert-based demo/self-check or one small test file; no frameworks, no fixtures). Trivial one-liners need no test.

(End of file - total 36 lines)
</content>

341: diff --git a/docs/cmd/inspect/index.md b/docs/cmd/inspect/index.md
342: index 2fe51f6..2a5b391 100644
343: --- a/docs/cmd/inspect/index.md
344: +++ b/docs/cmd/inspect/index.md
345: @@ -65,10 +65,20 @@ The data is provided in the context of a container that belongs to a containerla
346:  
347:  The `inspect` command produces a brief summary about the running lab components. It is also possible to get a full view on the running containers by adding `--details` flag.
348:  
349:  With this flag inspect command will output every bit of information about the running containers. This is what `docker inspect` command provides.
350:  
351: +#### containers
352: +
353: +By default `inspect` shows one entry per topology node.
354: +
355: +Nodes that consist of several containers (ie. distributed SR-SIM) are represented by a single node that carries the management addresses of the node.
356: +
357: +The local flag `--containers` will list every container of a lab rather than just the logical nodes.
358: +
359: +When the lab is selected with the `--topo` flag, only the containers of the nodes defined in that topology file are listed.
360: +
361:  #### wide
362:  
363:  The local `-w | --wide` flag adds all available columns to the `inspect` output table.
364:  
365:  ### Examples
366: diff --git a/docs/manual/kinds/srl.md b/docs/manual/kinds/srl.md
367: index 269d4ba..3aac436 100644
368: --- a/docs/manual/kinds/srl.md
369: +++ b/docs/manual/kinds/srl.md
370: @@ -468,11 +468,11 @@ The license file lifts these limitations as well as unlocks chassis-based platfo
371:  
372:  ### Reboot
373:  
374:  A reboot issued from within the node, for example with `tools platform chassis reboot`, restarts the SR Linux container. The node comes back with its links, saved configuration and management address intact.
375:  
376: -To support that, SR Linux nodes default to the `unless-stopped` [restart policy](../nodes.md#restart-policy), and containerlab keeps the links and the management address of each node in an internal `<node-name>-netns` container. The internal container is only listed by `containerlab inspect --all`, and it is removed together with the node.
377: +To support that, SR Linux nodes default to the `unless-stopped` [restart policy](../nodes.md#restart-policy), and containerlab keeps the links and the management address of each node in an internal `<node-name>-netns` container. The internal container is only listed by `containerlab inspect` with the [`--containers`](../../cmd/inspect/index.md#containers) or `--details` flag, and it is removed together with the node.
378:  
379:  Use `containerlab stop`, `start` and `restart` to manage the lifecycle of SR Linux nodes instead of restarting the containers with the container runtime directly.
380:  
381:  Nodes with a user-defined [`network-mode`](../nodes.md#network-mode) do not use the internal container.
382:

111: func inspectFn(cobraCmd *cobra.Command, o *Options) error {
112: 	if o.Global.TopologyName == "" && o.Global.TopologyFile == "" && !o.Destroy.All {
113: 		return fmt.Errorf(
114: 			"provide either a lab name (--name) or a topology file path (--topo) or the --all flag",
115: 		)
116: 	}
117: 
118: 	// Format validation (only relevant if --details is NOT used)
119: 	if !o.Inspect.Details &&
120: 		o.Inspect.Format != clabconstants.FormatTable &&
121: 		o.Inspect.Format != clabconstants.FormatJSON &&
122: 		o.Inspect.Format != clabconstants.FormatCSV {
123: 		return fmt.Errorf(
124: 			"output format %q is not supported when --details is not used, use "+
125: 				"'table', 'json' or 'csv'",
126: 			o.Inspect.Format,
127: 		)
128: 	}
129: 	// If --details is used, the format is implicitly JSON.
130: 	if o.Inspect.Details {
131: 		o.Inspect.Format = clabconstants.FormatJSON // Force JSON format if details are requested
132: 	}
133: 
134: 	c, err := clabcore.NewContainerLab(o.ToClabOptions()...)
135: 	if err != nil {
136: 		return err
137: 	}
138: 
139: 	containers, err := listContainers(cobraCmd.Context(), c, o)
140: 	if err != nil {
141: 		return err
142: 	}
143: 
144: 	// Handle empty results
145: 	if len(containers) == 0 {
146: 		switch o.Inspect.Format {
147: 		case clabconstants.FormatJSON:
148: 			fmt.Println("{}")
149: 		case clabconstants.FormatCSV:
150: 			fmt.Println(
151: 				"lab_name,labPath,absLabPath,name,container_id,image,kind,state,status," +
152: 					"ipv4_address,ipv6_address,owner",
153: 			)
154: 		default: // Table format
155: 			log.Info("no containers found")
156: 		}
157: 
158: 		return err
159: 	}
160: 
161: 	// Handle --details (always produces grouped JSON output)
162: 	if o.Inspect.Details {
163: 		return printContainerDetailsJSON(containers)
164: 	}
165: 
166: 	// Handle non-details cases (table or grouped JSON summary)
167: 	err = PrintContainerInspect(containers, o)
168: 
169: 	return err
170: }

172: // listContainers handles listing containers based on different criteria (topology or labels).
173: func listContainers(
174: 	ctx context.Context,
175: 	c *clabcore.CLab,
176: 	o *Options,
177: ) ([]clabruntime.GenericContainer, error) {
178: 	if c.LabRuntime != nil {
179: 		return c.ListLabRuntimeContainers(ctx, o.Destroy.All)
180: 	}
181: 
182: 	var listOptions []clabcore.ListOption
183: 
184: 	switch {
185: 	case o.Global.TopologyFile != "":
186: 		listOptions = append(listOptions, clabcore.WithListLabName(c.Config.Name))
187: 	case o.Global.TopologyName != "":
188: 		listOptions = append(listOptions, clabcore.WithListLabName(o.Global.TopologyName))
189: 	default:
190: 		listOptions = append(listOptions, clabcore.WithListclabLabelExists())
191: 	}
192: 
193: 	containers, err := c.ListContainers(ctx, listOptions...)
194: 	if err != nil {
195: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to list containers based on labels: %s", err)
196: 	}
197: 
198: 	if o.Global.TopologyFile != "" {
199: 		containers = slices.DeleteFunc(containers, func(ctr clabruntime.GenericContainer) bool {
200: 			_, isNode := c.Nodes[ctr.Labels[clabconstants.NodeName]]
201: 			_, isComponent := c.Nodes[ctr.Labels[clabconstants.RootNodeName]]
202: 
203: 			return !isNode && !isComponent
204: 		})
205: 
206: 		// containers that containerlab did not create (ie. ext-container) have no lab labels.
207: 		nodeContainers, err := c.ListNodesContainersIgnoreNotFound(ctx)
208: 		if err != nil {
209: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to list containers based on topology: %s", err)
210: 		}
211: 
212: 		for idx := range nodeContainers {
213: 			if !slices.ContainsFunc(containers, func(ctr clabruntime.GenericContainer) bool {
214: 				return ctr.ID == nodeContainers[idx].ID
215: 			}) {
216: 				containers = append(containers, nodeContainers[idx])
217: 			}
218: 		}
219: 	}
220: 
221: 	// --details always describes every container of a lab.
222: 	if o.Inspect.Containers || o.Inspect.Details {
223: 		return containers, nil
224: 	}
225: 
226: 	return logicalNodeContainers(containers), nil
227: }
228: 
229: // logicalNodeContainers returns a single logical topology node.
230: func logicalNodeContainers(
231: 	containers []clabruntime.GenericContainer,
232: ) []clabruntime.GenericContainer {
233: 	// Node names are unique only within a lab.
234: 	type nodeKey struct{ lab, node string }
235: 
236: 	holders := make(map[nodeKey]*clabruntime.GenericContainer)
237: 	hasCPMA := make(map[nodeKey]bool)
238: 
239: 	for idx := range containers {
240: 		l := containers[idx].Labels
241: 		key := nodeKey{l[clabconstants.Containerlab], l[clabconstants.RootNodeName]}
242: 
243: 		switch {
244: 		case key.node == "":
245: 		case l[clabconstants.InternalNode] == "true":
246: 			holders[key] = &containers[idx]
247: 		case l[clabconstants.NodeName] == key.node+"-a":
248: 			hasCPMA[key] = true
249: 		}
250: 	}
251: 
252: 	result := make([]clabruntime.GenericContainer, 0, len(containers))
253: 
254: 	for idx := range containers {
255: 		ctr := containers[idx]
256: 		name := ctr.Labels[clabconstants.NodeName]
257: 		key := nodeKey{
258: 			ctr.Labels[clabconstants.Containerlab],
259: 			ctr.Labels[clabconstants.RootNodeName],
260: 		}
261: 
262: 		// Components are named <root node>-<lowercase slot>.
263: 		isCPM := name == key.node+"-a" || (name == key.node+"-b" && !hasCPMA[key])
264: 		if ctr.Labels[clabconstants.ToolType] != "" ||
265: 			ctr.Labels[clabconstants.InternalNode] == "true" || (key.node != "" && !isCPM) {
266: 			continue
267: 		}
268: 
269: 		if key.node == "" {
270: 			key.node = name
271: 		}
272: 
273: 		if holder := holders[key]; holder != nil {
274: 			ctr.NetworkName = holder.NetworkName
275: 			ctr.NetworkSettings = holder.NetworkSettings
276: 			ctr.Ports = holder.Ports
277: 		}
278: 
279: 		result = append(result, ctr)
280: 	}
281: 
282: 	return result
283: }

285: func toTableData(contDetails []clabtypes.ContainerDetails, o *Options) []tableWriter.Row {
286: 	tabData := make([]tableWriter.Row, 0, len(contDetails))
287: 
288: 	for i := range contDetails {
289: 		d := &contDetails[i]
290: 		tabRow := tableWriter.Row{}
291: 
292: 		if o.Destroy.All {
293: 			tabRow = append(tabRow, d.LabPath, d.LabName)
294: 		}
295: 
296: 		if o.Inspect.Wide {
297: 			tabRow = append(tabRow, d.Owner)
298: 		}
299: 
300: 		// we do not want to print status other than health in the table view
301: 		if !strings.Contains(d.Status, "health") {
302: 			d.Status = ""
303: 		} else {
304: 			d.Status = fmt.Sprintf("(%s)", d.Status)
305: 		}
306: 
307: 		// Common fields
308: 		if o.Inspect.Wide {
309: 			// Print all fields on one line, no newlines
310: 			tabRow = append(tabRow,
311: 				d.Name,
312: 				fmt.Sprintf("%s %s", d.Kind, d.Image),
313: 				fmt.Sprintf("%s %s", d.State, d.Status),
314: 				fmt.Sprintf("%s %s",
315: 					ipWithoutPrefix(d.IPv4Address),
316: 					ipWithoutPrefix(d.IPv6Address)))
317: 		} else {
318: 			tabRow = append(tabRow,
319: 				d.Name,
320: 				fmt.Sprintf("%s\n%s", d.Kind, d.Image),
321: 				fmt.Sprintf("%s\n%s", d.State, d.Status),
322: 				fmt.Sprintf("%s\n%s",
323: 					ipWithoutPrefix(d.IPv4Address),
324: 					ipWithoutPrefix(d.IPv6Address)))
325: 		}
326: 
327: 		tabData = append(tabData, tabRow)
328: 	}
329: 
330: 	return tabData
331: }

333: // getShortestTopologyPath calculates the relative path to the provided topology file from
334: // the current working directory and returns it if it is shorted than the absolute path p.
335: func getShortestTopologyPath(p string) (string, error) {
336: 	if p == "" {
337: 		return "", nil
338: 	}
339: 	if strings.Contains(p, "://") {
340: 		return p, nil
341: 	}
342: 
343: 	// get topo file path relative of the cwd
344: 	cwd, err := os.Getwd()
345: 	if err != nil {
346: 		return "", err
347: 	}
348: 
349: 	relPath, err := filepath.Rel(cwd, p)
350: 	if err != nil {
351: 		return "", err
352: 	}
353: 
354: 	if len(relPath) < len(p) {
355: 		return relPath, nil
356: 	}
357: 
358: 	return p, nil
359: }

361: // printContainerDetailsJSON handles the detailed JSON output of containers grouped by lab name.
362: func printContainerDetailsJSON(containers []clabruntime.GenericContainer) error {
363: 	groupedDetails := make(map[string][]clabruntime.GenericContainer)
364: 	// Sort containers first by lab name, then by container name for consistent output
365: 	sort.Slice(containers, func(i, j int) bool {
366: 		labNameI := containers[i].Labels[clabconstants.Containerlab]
367: 		labNameJ := containers[j].Labels[clabconstants.Containerlab]
368: 
369: 		if labNameI == labNameJ {
370: 			// Use the first name if available
371: 			nameI := ""
372: 			if len(containers[i].Names) > 0 {
373: 				nameI = containers[i].Names[0]
374: 			}
375: 
376: 			nameJ := ""
377: 			if len(containers[j].Names) > 0 {
378: 				nameJ = containers[j].Names[0]
379: 			}
380: 
381: 			return nameI < nameJ
382: 		}
383: 
384: 		return labNameI < labNameJ
385: 	})
386: 
387: 	// Group the sorted containers
388: 	for idx := range containers {
389: 		labName := containers[idx].Labels[clabconstants.Containerlab]
390: 		// Ensure labName exists, default to a placeholder if missing
391: 		// (shouldn't happen with filters)
392: 		if labName == "" {
393: 			labName = "_unknown_lab_"
394: 		}
395: 
396: 		groupedDetails[labName] = append(groupedDetails[labName], containers[idx])
397: 	}
398: 
399: 	b, err := json.MarshalIndent(groupedDetails, "", "  ")
400: 	if err != nil {
401: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal grouped container details: %v", err)
402: 	}
403: 
404: 	fmt.Println(string(b))
405: 
406: 	return nil
407: }

409: func printContainerInspectJSON(contDetails []clabtypes.ContainerDetails) error {
410: 	// Group summary results by LabName
411: 	// Use a map where keys are lab names and values are slices of container details
412: 	groupedLabs := make(map[string][]clabtypes.ContainerDetails)
413: 
414: 	for idx := range contDetails {
415: 		labName := contDetails[idx].LabName
416: 		if labName == "" {
417: 			labName = "_unknown_lab_" // Should not happen if filters work correctly
418: 		}
419: 		// Assign the *entire* ContainerDetails struct (including AbsLabPath)
420: 		groupedLabs[labName] = append(groupedLabs[labName], contDetails[idx])
421: 	}
422: 
423: 	b, err := json.MarshalIndent(groupedLabs, "", "  ")
424: 	if err != nil {
425: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal grouped container summary: %v", err)
426: 	}
427: 
428: 	fmt.Println(string(b))
429: 
430: 	return nil
431: }

433: func printContainerInspectTable(contDetails []clabtypes.ContainerDetails, o *Options) {
434: 	// Generate and render table using the summary data (which uses relative LabPath)
435: 	tabData := toTableData(contDetails, o)
436: 	table := tableWriter.NewWriter()
437: 	table.SetOutputMirror(os.Stdout)
438: 	table.SetStyle(tableWriter.StyleRounded)
439: 	table.Style().Format.Header = text.FormatTitle
440: 	table.Style().Format.HeaderAlign = text.AlignCenter
441: 	table.Style().Options.SeparateRows = true
442: 	table.Style().Color = tableWriter.ColorOptions{
443: 		Header: text.Colors{text.Bold},
444: 	}
445: 
446: 	headerBase := tableWriter.Row{"Name", "Kind/Image", "State", "IPv4/6 Address"}
447: 	if o.Inspect.Wide {
448: 		headerBase = slices.Insert(headerBase, 0, "Owner")
449: 	}
450: 
451: 	var header tableWriter.Row
452: 
453: 	var colConfigs []tableWriter.ColumnConfig
454: 
455: 	// Lab-level columns (Topology, Lab Name, Owner) AutoMerge across nodes of the same lab.
456: 	if o.Destroy.All {
457: 		header = append(tableWriter.Row{"Topology", "Lab Name"}, headerBase...)
458: 		colConfigs = append(
459: 			colConfigs,
460: 			tableWriter.ColumnConfig{
461: 				Number:    1,
462: 				AutoMerge: true, VAlign: text.VAlignMiddle,
463: 			},
464: 			tableWriter.ColumnConfig{
465: 				Number:    2, //nolint: mnd
466: 				AutoMerge: true, VAlign: text.VAlignMiddle,
467: 			},
468: 		)
469: 		if o.Inspect.Wide {
470: 			colConfigs = append(colConfigs, tableWriter.ColumnConfig{
471: 				Number:    3, //nolint: mnd
472: 				AutoMerge: true, VAlign: text.VAlignMiddle,
473: 			})
474: 		}
475: 	} else {
476: 		header = headerBase
477: 
478: 		colConfigs = append(colConfigs, tableWriter.ColumnConfig{
479: 			Number:    1,
480: 			AutoMerge: true, VAlign: text.VAlignMiddle,
481: 		})
482: 	}
483: 
484: 	table.AppendHeader(header)
485: 
486: 	if len(colConfigs) > 0 {
487: 		table.SetColumnConfigs(colConfigs)
488: 	}
489: 
490: 	table.AppendRows(tabData)
491: 	table.Render()
492: }

516: // PrintContainerInspect handles non-details output (table or grouped JSON summary).
517: func PrintContainerInspect(containers []clabruntime.GenericContainer, o *Options) error {
518: 	contDetails := make([]clabtypes.ContainerDetails, 0, len(containers))
519: 
520: 	// Gather summary details of each container
521: 	for idx := range containers {
522: 		absPath := containers[idx].Labels[clabconstants.TopoFile]
523: 
524: 		shortPath, err := getShortestTopologyPath(absPath)
525: 		if err != nil {
526: 			log.Warnf(
527: 				"failed to get relative topology path for container %s: %v, using raw path %q",
528: 				containers[idx].Names[0],
529: 				err,
530: 				absPath,
531: 			)
532: 
533: 			shortPath = absPath // Use raw path as fallback for display
534: 		}
535: 
536: 		status := parseStatus(containers[idx].Status)
537: 
538: 		cdet := clabtypes.ContainerDetails{
539: 			LabName:     containers[idx].Labels[clabconstants.Containerlab],
540: 			LabPath:     shortPath, // Relative or shortest path for table view
541: 			AbsLabPath:  absPath,   // Absolute path for JSON view
542: 			Image:       containers[idx].Image,
543: 			State:       containers[idx].State,
544: 			Status:      status,
545: 			IPv4Address: containers[idx].GetContainerIPv4(),
546: 			IPv6Address: containers[idx].GetContainerIPv6(),
547: 			ContainerID: containers[idx].ShortID,
548: 			// Only lab runtimes set the workload; it adds namespace, pod, container, node_uid,
549: 			// exposed_ports and load_balancer_address to the JSON output.
550: 			LabRuntimeWorkload: containers[idx].Workload,
551: 		}
552: 
553: 		if len(containers[idx].Names) > 0 {
554: 			cdet.Name = containers[idx].Names[0]
555: 		}
556: 
557: 		if group, ok := containers[idx].Labels[clabconstants.NodeGroup]; ok {
558: 			cdet.Group = group
559: 		}
560: 
561: 		if kind, ok := containers[idx].Labels[clabconstants.NodeKind]; ok {
562: 			cdet.Kind = kind
563: 		}
564: 
565: 		if owner, ok := containers[idx].Labels[clabconstants.Owner]; ok {
566: 			cdet.Owner = owner
567: 		}
568: 
569: 		contDetails = append(contDetails, cdet)
570: 	}
571: 
572: 	// Sort summary details by lab name, then container name
573: 	sort.Slice(contDetails, func(i, j int) bool {
574: 		if contDetails[i].LabName == contDetails[j].LabName {
575: 			return contDetails[i].Name < contDetails[j].Name
576: 		}
577: 
578: 		return contDetails[i].LabName < contDetails[j].LabName
579: 	})
580: 
581: 	switch o.Inspect.Format {
582: 	case clabconstants.FormatJSON:
583: 		err := printContainerInspectJSON(contDetails)
584: 		if err != nil {
585: 			return err
586: 		}
587: 	case "table":
588: 		printContainerInspectTable(contDetails, o)
589: 	case "csv":
590: 		printContainerInspectCSV(contDetails)
591: 	default:
592: 		return fmt.Errorf("internal error: unhandled format %q", o.Inspect.Format)
593: 	}
594: 
595: 	return nil
596: }

598: // parseStatus extracts a simpler status string, focusing on health states.
599: func parseStatus(status string) string {
600: 	switch {
601: 	case strings.Contains(status, "unhealthy"):
602: 		return "unhealthy"
603: 	case strings.Contains(status, "health: starting"):
604: 		return "health: starting"
605: 	case strings.Contains(status, "healthy"):
606: 		return "healthy"
607: 	default:
608: 		// Return original status if no specific health info found
609: 		return status
610: 	}
611: }
612: 
613: // ipWithoutPrefix removes the CIDR prefix length from an IP address string.
614: // Returns "N/A" if input contains "N/A".
615: // Returns original string if it doesn't contain exactly one "/".
616: func ipWithoutPrefix(ip string) string {
617: 	if strings.Contains(ip, clabconstants.NotApplicable) {
618: 		return ip
619: 	}
620: 
621: 	ipParts := strings.Split(ip, "/")
622: 	if len(ipParts) != 2 { //nolint: mnd
623: 		return ip // Return original if not in expected format "address/prefix"
624: 	}
625: 
626: 	return ipParts[0]
627: }

19: 		}
20: 
21: 		if internal {
22: 			labels[clabconstants.InternalNode] = "true"
23: 		}
24: 
25: 		return clabruntime.GenericContainer{
26: 			Names:           []string{"clab-" + lab + "-" + name},
27: 			Labels:          labels,
28: 			NetworkSettings: clabruntime.GenericMgmtIPs{IPv4addr: ip},
29: 		}
30: 	}
31: 
32: 	tool := ctr("lab1", "", "", false, "10.0.0.9")
33: 	tool.Labels[clabconstants.ToolType] = "sshx"
34: 
35: 	got := logicalNodeContainers([]clabruntime.GenericContainer{
36: 		tool,
37: 		// internal node without a root node.
38: 		ctr("lab1", "tailscale", "", true, "10.0.0.8"),
39: 		ctr("lab1", "linux", "", false, "10.0.0.1"),
40: 		// SR Linux node with a netns holder.
41: 		ctr("lab1", "srl", "", false, ""),
42: 		ctr("lab1", "srl-netns", "srl", true, "10.0.0.2"),
43: 		// distributed SR-SIM node.
44: 		ctr("lab1", "sr-1", "sr", false, ""),
45: 		ctr("lab1", "sr-b", "sr", false, ""),
46: 		ctr("lab1", "sr-a", "sr", false, ""),
47: 		ctr("lab1", "sr-netns", "sr", true, "10.0.0.3"),
48: 		// distributed SR-SIM node without CPM A, and a node name shared with lab1.
49: 		ctr("lab2", "sr-1", "sr", false, ""),
50: 		ctr("lab2", "sr-b", "sr", false, ""),
51: 		ctr("lab2", "sr-netns", "sr", true, "10.0.0.4"),
52: 		ctr("lab2", "linux", "", false, "10.0.0.5"),
53: 	})
54: 
55: 	want := []string{
56: 		"clab-lab1-linux 10.0.0.1",
57: 		"clab-lab1-srl 10.0.0.2",
58: 		"clab-lab1-sr-a 10.0.0.3",
59: 		"clab-lab2-sr-b 10.0.0.4",
60: 		"clab-lab2-linux 10.0.0.5",
61: 	}
62: 
63: 	gotRows := make([]string, 0, len(got))
64: 	for idx := range got {
65: 		gotRows = append(gotRows, got[idx].Names[0]+" "+got[idx].NetworkSettings.IPv4addr)
66: 	}
67: 
68: 	if !slices.Equal(gotRows, want) {
69: 		t.Fatalf("logical node containers mismatch\n got: %v\nwant: %v", gotRows, want)
70: 	}
71: }

1: package core

16: // ListContainers lists all containers using provided filter.
17: func (c *CLab) ListContainers(
18: 	ctx context.Context,
19: 	options ...ListOption,
20: ) ([]clabruntime.GenericContainer, error) {
21: 	opts := NewListOptions()
22: 
23: 	for _, opt := range options {
24: 		opt(opts)
25: 	}
26: 
27: 	var containers []clabruntime.GenericContainer
28: 
29: 	for _, r := range c.Runtimes {
30: 		ctrs, err := r.ListContainers(ctx, opts.ToFilters())
31: 		if err != nil {
32: 			return containers, fmt.Errorf("could not list containers: %v", err)
33: 		}
34: 
35: 		containers = append(containers, ctrs...)
36: 	}
37: 
38: 	return containers, nil
39: }
40: 
41: // ListNodesContainers lists all containers based on the nodes stored in clab instance.
42: func (c *CLab) ListNodesContainers(
43: 	ctx context.Context,
44: ) ([]clabruntime.GenericContainer, error) {
45: 	var containers []clabruntime.GenericContainer
46: 
47: 	for _, n := range c.Nodes {
48: 		cts, err := n.GetContainers(ctx)
49: 		if err != nil {
50: 			return containers, fmt.Errorf(
51: 				"could not get container for node %s: %v",
52: 				n.Config().LongName, err,
53: 			)
54: 		}
55: 
56: 		containers = append(containers, cts...)
57: 	}
58: 
59: 	return containers, nil
60: }
61: 
62: // ListNodesContainersIgnoreNotFound lists all containers based on the nodes stored in clab
63: // instance, ignoring errors for non found containers.
64: func (c *CLab) ListNodesContainersIgnoreNotFound(
65: 	ctx context.Context,
66: ) ([]clabruntime.GenericContainer, error) {
67: 	var containers []clabruntime.GenericContainer
68: 
69: 	for _, n := range c.Nodes {
70: 		cts, err := n.GetContainers(ctx)
71: 		if err != nil {
72: 			continue
73: 		}
74: 
75: 		containers = append(containers, cts...)
76: 	}
77: 
78: 	return containers, nil
79: }

81: // ListContainerInterfaces list interfaces of the given container.
82: func (c *CLab) ListContainerInterfaces(
83: 	ctx context.Context,
84: 	container *clabruntime.GenericContainer,
85: ) (*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaces, error) {
86: 	containerInterfaces := clabtypes.ContainerInterfaces{}
87: 
88: 	if len(container.Names) > 0 {
89: 		containerInterfaces.ContainerName = container.Names[0]
90: 	}
91: 
92: 	// Retrieve the path to the container network NS
93: 	nodeNsPath, err := container.Runtime.GetNSPath(ctx, containerInterfaces.ContainerName)
94: 	if err != nil {
95: 		return nil, err
96: 	}
97: 
98: 	// Get network NS handle
99: 	var containerNsHandle netns.NsHandle
100: 
101: 	switch {
102: 	case nodeNsPath != "":
103: 		containerNsHandle, err = netns.GetFromPath(nodeNsPath)
104: 		if err != nil {
105: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unable to get container network NS handle: %w", err)
106: 		}
107: 		defer containerNsHandle.Close()
108: 	case container.Runtime.GetName() == "podman":
109: 		// Network NS path is empty and the runtime is Podman -> host network mode
110: 		// Manually get the handle for the root network namespace
111: 		containerNsHandle, err = netns.Get()
112: 		if err != nil {
113: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unable to get root network NS handle: %w", err)
114: 		}
115: 		defer containerNsHandle.Close()
116: 	default:
117: 		log.Warnf("Container %v has no namespace set, skipping!", containerInterfaces.ContainerName)
118: 		containerInterfaces.Interfaces = make([]*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaceDetails, 0)
119: 
120: 		return &containerInterfaces, nil
121: 	}
122: 
123: 	// Get Netlink handle in container network NS
124: 	netlinkHandle, err := netlink.NewHandleAt(containerNsHandle)
125: 	if err != nil {
126: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unable to enter container network NS: %w", err)
127: 	}
128: 	defer netlinkHandle.Close()
129: 
130: 	interfaces, err := netlinkHandle.LinkList()
131: 	if err != nil {
132: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unable to list network interfaces: %w", err)
133: 	}
134: 
135: 	containerInterfaces.Interfaces = make(
136: 		[]*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaceDetails,
137: 		0,
138: 		len(interfaces),
139: 	)
140: 
141: 	lab, node := TopoIdentity(container.Labels)
142: 
143: 	for _, iface := range interfaces {
144: 		reported, alias := reportedInterface(iface, lab, node)
145: 		attrs := reported.Attrs()
146: 
147: 		ifaceDetails := clabtypes.ContainerInterfaceDetails{
148: 			InterfaceName:  attrs.Name,
149: 			InterfaceAlias: alias,
150: 			InterfaceMTU:   attrs.MTU,
151: 			InterfaceMAC:   attrs.HardwareAddr.String(),
152: 			InterfaceIndex: attrs.Index,
153: 			InterfaceType:  reported.Type(),
154: 			InterfaceState: attrs.OperState.String(),
155: 		}
156: 		log.Debugf("Interface info: %+v", ifaceDetails)
157: 
158: 		containerInterfaces.Interfaces = append(containerInterfaces.Interfaces, &ifaceDetails)
159: 	}
160: 
161: 	log.Debugf("Fetched %v interfaces for %v", len(interfaces), containerInterfaces.ContainerName)
162: 
163: 	return &containerInterfaces, nil
164: }
165: 
166: // reportedInterface substitutes the host-side stitch interface for iface when
167: // one exists, keeping the topology name as alias so the swap is transparent.
168: func reportedInterface(iface netlink.Link, lab, node string) (netlink.Link, string) {
169: 	alias := iface.Attrs().Alias
170: 
171: 	topoName := alias
172: 	if topoName == "" {
173: 		topoName = iface.Attrs().Name
174: 	}
175: 
176: 	if tools, ok := clablinks.ToolsInterface(lab, node, topoName); ok {
177: 		return tools, topoName
178: 	}
179: 
180: 	return iface, alias
181: }
182: 
183: // ListContainersInterfaces list interfaces of all given containers.
184: func (c *CLab) ListContainersInterfaces(
185: 	ctx context.Context,
186: 	containers []clabruntime.GenericContainer,
187: ) ([]*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaces, error) {
188: 	containerInterfaces := make([]*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaces, 0, len(containers))
189: 
190: 	for idx := range containers {
191: 		cIfs, err := c.ListContainerInterfaces(ctx, &containers[idx])
192: 		if err != nil {
193: 			containerName := ""
194: 			if len(containers[idx].Names) > 0 {
195: 				containerName = containers[idx].Names[0]
196: 			}
197: 			log.Warn("Skipping interface detection", "node", containerName, "err", err)
198: 			continue
199: 		}
200: 
201: 		if len(cIfs.Interfaces) > 0 {
202: 			sort.Slice(cIfs.Interfaces, func(i, j int) bool {
203: 				return cIfs.Interfaces[i].InterfaceName < cIfs.Interfaces[j].InterfaceName
204: 			})
205: 		} else {
206: 			log.Warnf("No interfaces found for container %v", cIfs.ContainerName)
207: 		}
208: 
209: 		containerInterfaces = append(containerInterfaces, cIfs)
210: 	}
211: 
212: 	sort.Slice(containerInterfaces, func(i, j int) bool {
213: 		return containerInterfaces[i].ContainerName < containerInterfaces[j].ContainerName
214: 	})
215: 
216: 	return containerInterfaces, nil
217: }

What about tool containers (sshx) when using -t? They'd be removed by the DeleteFunc if neither their NodeName nor RootNodeName is in c.Nodes. But with --all or --name, tools are included in the label list, and logicalNodeContainers skips them by ToolType. With --containers + -t, tools would be filtered out by DeleteFunc but might be re-added by ListNodesContainersIgnoreNotFound? No — tools aren't topology nodes. So `inspect -t --containers` doesn't show tools, while `inspect --all --containers` does. Inconsistency, minor. Actually wait — is that a behavior change vs base? Base -t used ListNodesContainersIgnoreNotFound → only node containers → tools not shown with -t in base either. So consistent with base.

Scenario: lab has a node named "x-a" (regular linux node). Container NodeName=x-a, no RootNodeName → key.node="" → included. Good.

Scenario: distributed node "sr" in lab, and ANOTHER regular node named "sr-a"? Node names must be unique; "sr-a" as a separate topology node is possible! E.g., topo has node `sr` (srsim distributed) and node `sr-a` (linux). Then:

- Second pass: linux node sr-a: key={lab,""} → included once. Component sr-a: key={lab,"sr"} → isCPM true → included. So "sr-a" appears twice — once as the linux logical node and once as the CPM. 180: func (c *CLab) deploy( //nolint: funlen
181: 	ctx context.Context,
182: 	options *DeployOptions,
183: ) ([]clabruntime.GenericContainer, error) {
184: 	if c.LabRuntime != nil {
185: 		return c.deployWithLabRuntime(ctx, options)
186: 	}
187: 
188: 	var err error
189: 
190: 	err = c.ResolveLinks()
191: 	if err != nil {
192: 		return nil, err
193: 	}
194: 
195: 	log.Debugf("lab Conf: %+v", c.Config)
196: 
197: 	if options.reconfigure {
198: 		_ = c.destroy(ctx, uint(len(c.Nodes)), true)
199: 		log.Info("Removing directory", "path", c.TopoPaths.TopologyLabDir())
200: 
201: 		if err := os.RemoveAll(c.TopoPaths.TopologyLabDir()); err != nil {
202: 			return nil, err
203: 		}
204: 	}
205: 
206: 	err = c.prepareLabManagementNetwork(ctx)
207: 	if err != nil {
208: 		return nil, err
209: 	}
210: 
211: 	if err := c.checkTopologyDefinition(ctx); err != nil {
212: 		return nil, err
213: 	}
214: 
215: 	if err := c.prepareDeployArtifacts(ctx, options.skipLabDirFileACLs); err != nil {
216: 		return nil, err
217: 	}
218: 
219: 	// Apply snapshot restore configuration to nodes
220: 	if err := c.configureSnapshotRestore(options); err != nil {
221: 		return nil, err
222: 	}
223: 
224: 	nodesWg, execCollection, nodeFailCh, err := c.createNodes(
225: 		ctx,
226: 		options.maxWorkers,
227: 		options.skipPostDeploy,
228: 	)
229: 	if err != nil {
230: 		return nil, err
231: 	}
232: 
233: 	if err := waitForNodeDeploy(ctx, nodesWg, nodeFailCh); err != nil {
234: 		return nil, err
235: 	}
236: 	if err := c.syncTailscaleProxy(ctx); err != nil {
237: 		return nil, err
238: 	}
239: 	if err := c.SyncMgmtHostRoutes(ctx); err != nil {
240: 		return nil, err
241: 	}
242: 
243: 	// also call deploy on the special nodes endpoints (only host is required for the
244: 	// vxlan stitched endpoints).
245: 	// this must happen after all node workers have finished so that veth pairs created
246: 	// as part of vxlan-stitch links are already deployed before the stitch TC rules are applied.
247: 	eps := c.getSpecialLinkNodes()["host"].GetEndpoints()
248: 	for _, ep := range eps {
249: 		err = ep.Deploy(ctx)
250: 		if err != nil {
251: 			log.Warnf("failed deploying endpoint %s", ep)
252: 		}
253: 	}
254: 
255: 	// Stitch links after node workers and host endpoints have finished.
256: 	// The veth pair is already created by node workers and the VxLAN interface is created
257: 	// by host endpoint deploy; Stitch applies the TC redirect rules to bridge them.
258: 	var linkPostDeployWorkers errgroup.Group
259: 	linkPostDeployWorkers.SetLimit(int(options.maxWorkers))
260: 	for _, link := range c.Links {
261: 		linkPostDeployWorkers.Go(func() error {
262: 			if err := link.PostDeploy(ctx); err != nil {
263: 				log.Warnf("failed post-deploying link: %v", err)
264: 			}
265: 			return nil
266: 		})
267: 	}
268: 	_ = linkPostDeployWorkers.Wait()
269: 
270: 	execCollection.Log()
271: 
272: 	containers, err := c.finalize(ctx, options.exportTemplate, options.graph)
273: 	if err != nil {
274: 		return nil, err
275: 	}
276: 
277: 	// set after finalizing, so a failed impairment doesn't skip the lab's exports and state
278: 	if err := clablinks.ApplyLinkImpairments(ctx, linksEndpoints(c.Links)); err != nil {
279: 		return nil, err
280: 	}
281: 
282: 	return containers, nil
283: }

285: func waitForNodeDeploy(
286: 	ctx context.Context,
287: 	nodesWg *sync.WaitGroup,
288: 	nodeFailCh chan error,
289: ) error {
290: 	if nodesWg != nil {
291: 		nodesWg.Wait()
292: 	}
293: 
294: 	close(nodeFailCh)
295: 
296: 	// Cancellation takes precedence over errors caused by workers unwinding, and
297: 	// prevents post-deploy work from running against a partial lab.
298: 	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
299: 		return err
300: 	}
301: 
302: 	var nodeFailErrs []error
303: 	for nodeErr := range nodeFailCh {
304: 		nodeFailErrs = append(nodeFailErrs, nodeErr)
305: 	}
306: 	if len(nodeFailErrs) > 0 {
307: 		return fmt.Errorf(
308: 			"deployment failed for one or more nodes: %w",
309: 			errors.Join(nodeFailErrs...),
310: 		)
311: 	}
312: 
313: 	return nil
314: }

379: }

265: 	if !exists {

267: 	}
268: 	n, err := c.Reg.NewNodeOfKind(nodeCfg.Kind)

271: 	}

276: 	); err != nil {
277: 		return fmt.Errorf("initializing node %q: %w", nodeCfg.ShortName, err)
278: 	}
279: 
280: 	if c.Nodes == nil {
281: 		c.Nodes = make(map[string]clabnodes.Node)
282: 	}
283: 	c.Nodes[nodeCfg.ShortName] = n
284:

121: 	return n.netnsNode.GetContainerStatus(ctx) == clabruntime.NotFound &&

127: 	if n.netnsNode == nil || n.deployedWithoutNetnsNode(ctx) {
128: 		return n.DefaultNode.GetNSPath(ctx)
129: 	}
130: 
131: 	return n.netnsNode.GetNSPath(ctx)
132: }

139:

49: // createLabelsMap creates container labels map for additional containers launched after the lab
50: // is up. Such as sshx, gotty, etc.
51: func createLabelsMap(topo, labName, containerName, owner, toolType string) map[string]string {
52: 	shortName := strings.Replace(containerName, "clab-"+labName+"-", "", 1)
53: 
54: 	labels := map[string]string{
55: 		clabconstants.Containerlab: labName,
56: 		clabconstants.NodeName:     shortName,
57: 		clabconstants.LongName:     containerName,
58: 		clabconstants.NodeKind:     "linux",
59: 		clabconstants.NodeGroup:    "",
60: 		clabconstants.NodeType:     "tool",
61: 		clabconstants.ToolType:     toolType,
62: 	}
63: 
64: 	// Add topology file path
65: 	if topo != "" {
66: 		absPath, err := filepath.Abs(topo)
67: 		if err == nil {
68: 			labels[clabconstants.TopoFile] = absPath
69: 		} else {
70: 			labels[clabconstants.TopoFile] = topo
71: 		}
72: 
73: 		// Set node lab directory
74: 		baseDir := filepath.Dir(topo)
75: 		labels[clabconstants.NodeLabDir] = filepath.Join(baseDir, "clab-"+labName, shortName)
76: 	}
77: 
78: 	// Add owner label if available
79: 	if owner != "" {
80: 		labels[clabconstants.Owner] = owner
81: 	}
82: 
83: 	return labels
84: }

Reasoning
Tool containers (sshx, gotty, api-server) carry `NodeName` = short name like "sshx", not present in c.Nodes; no RootNodeName. So in the -t path DeleteFunc: `isNode = c.Nodes["sshx"]` fails, `isComponent = c.Nodes[""]` fails → removed. Good — tools are excluded from -t inspect. And in --all/--name path, tools are in the label list but skipped by ToolType in logicalNodeContainers. But with `--containers` and --all, tools ARE shown. Consistent enough.

Now key remaining question: does the -t path's label-based list actually find the right containers? `WithListLabName(c.Config.Name)`. Wait — there's a subtlety: c.Config.Name for a topology file. Fine.

But there is a real behavioral consideration for -t: in base, `inspect -t` listed ONLY the containers of nodes in the topology (via ListNodesContainersIgnoreNotFound), which for the srsim node returns the CPM A container (with distNodeMgmtIPs override) — so base -t output showed sr14s-a with the mgmt IP. And the internal holder was filtered out by the `!o.Destroy.All` DeleteFunc in listContainers... wait, base -t path: ListNodesContainersIgnoreNotFound — for a distributed srsim node, GetContainers returns the CPM A container, NOT the holder (holder only returned as fallback). So base -t never showed the holder unless CPM not found. And base's internal filter would remove the holder if it appeared. OK.

New -t: label list + node list merged, then logicalNodeContainers. Result: sr14s-a (CPM) with holder network settings copied. Wait — but ListNodesContainers for sros node already sets NetworkSettings to distNodeMgmtIPs (via GetContainers forge). And logicalNodeContainers copies the holder's settings over — same values presumably. Fine.

Now — the important question about the second-pass skip logic in logicalNodeContainers:

```go
isCPM := name == key.node+"-a" || (name == key.node+"-b" && !hasCPMA[key])
if ctr.Labels[ToolType] != "" ||
    ctr.Labels[InternalNode] == "true" || (key.node != "" && !isCPM) {
    continue
}
```

Wait — this is inverted from what I'd expect: the FIRST pass records holders and hasCPMA. The SECOND pass iterates ALL containers again, and for internal nodes it hits `ctr.Labels[InternalNode] == "true"` → skipped. But then how do the holder's network settings get to the logical node? Via the holders map — `if holder := holders[key]; holder != nil` copies NetworkName/NetworkSettings/Ports. Good.

Now, a question: what about the SR Linux node with a netns holder, where c.Nodes contains "srl" and GetContainers (node path) returns the srl container with holder network settings already? In the -t path with logicalNodeContainers, for the srl container: name="srl", key={lab,""} (no RootNodeName on the srl container) → included, key.node="srl", holders[{lab,"srl"}] = the holder container → overwrite NetworkSettings with holder's — same values. Good.

But wait — there's a real bug candidate here: `holders` map is keyed by `nodeKey{l[Containerlab], l[RootNodeName]}`. For the srl case, the holder has RootNodeName="srl", so key={lab,"srl"} and holders[{lab,"srl"}] set. In the second pass, the srl container has RootNodeName="" → key={lab,""} → after `if key.node == "" { key.node = name }` → key={lab,"srl"} → holders lookup succeeds. Good — that's why the key.node reassignment happens before the holders lookup.

Now for the CPM A container: RootNodeName="sr" → key={lab,"sr"}; isCPM: name "sr-a" == "sr-a" → true → included; holders[{lab,"sr"}] = sr-netns → copy. Good.

CPM B (when A exists): skipped. Line card sr-1: key.node="sr", isCPM false → skipped. Good.

Now, first-pass hasCPMA detection: `case l[NodeName] == key.node+"-a"`. This is evaluated for non-internal containers with root set. But note: the first-pass switch only sets hasCPMA when the container ALSO is not internal. Fine.

Edge: what if the lab has a distributed srsim node "sr" AND a regular node named "sr-a" (as discussed)? Then second pass: regular node "sr-a" (no root) → included once with key={lab,""} → key.node="sr-a" → holders[{lab,"sr-a"}] — nil (holders keyed by root "sr") → included. And CPM sr-a → included with key={lab,"sr"}. Duplicate names "clab-lab-sr-a" twice. Edge case, user-invited collision. Also the hasCPMA map would be true (set by the regular node? No — first pass: regular node "sr-a" has key={lab,""} → case key.node=="" → skipped; so hasCPMA only set by the component). Fine.

Now, what about a distributed srsim node where CPM slots are named with the node's own name e.g. node "r1" with components A and B → "r1-a", "r1-b". OK.

What about `hasCPMA` when the CPM A container is present but the topology has no components (standalone)? Not relevant.

Now, the case where the distributed sros node's CPM A container is down/removed: the sros GetContainers falls back to the holder. In the -t label path, the label list would contain the holder (InternalNode) and the second pass would skip it (InternalNode == true) → the logical node disappears from inspect. In base, the fallback holder was also filtered out (InternalNode) → same behavior. OK consistent.

Now, the deploy summary: result.Containers from ListNodesContainers. For a distributed srsim, the node returns the CPM A container → summary lists "sr-a". Test expects "linux sr-a". Good. And for the srl node, returns the srl container with holder's net settings. Summary lists "linux srl". Test expects that. Good.

Wait, but why did deployFn need the DeleteFunc at all if PrintContainerInspect previously did the filtering? Because PrintContainerInspect's filter was removed in this PR. Why remove it? Because with `--containers`/`--details` from inspect, internal containers must be printed. The filter was tied to `!o.Destroy.All` — the new logic is `o.Inspect.Containers || o.Inspect.Details`. But deployFn doesn't have --containers flag... actually deploy uses o.Inspect.Format? Deploy's Options includes Inspect options. The deploy summary needs to always hide internal containers, hence the filter moved to deployFn. And labruntime_gaps_test.go calls PrintContainerInspect directly — need to check whether it relies on the internal filtering. Let me read that test.

345: @@ -65,10 +65,20 @@ The data is provided in the context of a container that belongs to a containerla
346:  
347:  The `inspect` command produces a brief summary about the running lab components. It is also possible to get a full view on the running containers by adding `--details` flag.
348:  
349:  With this flag inspect command will output every bit of information about the running containers. This is what `docker inspect` command provides.
350:  
351: +#### containers
352: +
353: +By default `inspect` shows one entry per topology node.
354: +
355: +Nodes that consist of several containers (ie. distributed SR-SIM) are represented by a single node that carries the management addresses of the node.
356: +
357: +The local flag `--containers` will list every container of a lab rather than just the logical nodes.
358: +
359: +When the lab is selected with the `--topo` flag, only the containers of the nodes defined in that topology file are listed.
360: +
361:  #### wide
362:  
363:  The local `-w | --wide` flag adds all available columns to the `inspect` output table.
364:  
365:  ### Examples

371:  
372:  ### Reboot
373:  
374:  A reboot issued from within the node, for example with `tools platform chassis reboot`, restarts the SR Linux container. The node comes back with its links, saved configuration and management address intact.
375:

The internal container is only listed by `containerlab inspect --all`, and it is removed together with the node.
377: +To support that, SR Linux nodes default to the `unless-stopped` [restart policy](../nodes.md#restart-policy), and containerlab keeps the links and the management address of each node in an internal `<node-name>-netns` container. The internal container is only listed by `containerlab inspect` with the [`--containers`](../../cmd/inspect/index.md#containers) or `--details` flag, and it is removed together with the node.
378:  
379:  Use `containerlab stop`, `start` and `restart` to manage the lifecycle of SR Linux nodes instead of restarting the containers with the container runtime directly.
380:  
381:  Nodes with a user-defined [`network-mode`](../nodes.md#network-mode) do not use the internal container.

It is also possible to get a full view on the running containers by adding `--details` flag.\n \n With this flag inspect command will output every bit of information about the running containers. This is what `docker inspect` command provides.\n \n+#### containers\n+\n+By default `inspect` shows one entry per topology node.\n+\n+Nodes that consist of several containers (ie. distributed SR-SIM) are represented by a single node that carries the management addresses of the node.\n+\n+The local flag `--containers` will list every container of a lab rather than just the logical nodes.\n+\n+When the lab is selected with the `--topo` flag, only the containers of the nodes defined in that topology file are listed.\n+\n #### wide\n \n The local `-w | --wide` flag adds all available columns to the `inspect` output table.\n \n ### Examples\ndiff --git a/docs/manual/kinds/srl.md b/docs/manual/kinds/srl.md\nindex 269d4ba..3aac436 100644\n--- a/docs/manual/kinds/srl.md\n+++ b/docs/manual/kinds/srl.md\n@@ -468,11 +468,11 @@ The license file lifts these limitations as well as unlocks chassis-based platfo\n \n ### Reboot\n \n A reboot issued from within the node, for example with `tools platform chassis reboot`, restarts the SR Linux container. The node comes back with its links, saved configuration and management address intact.\n \n-To support that, SR Linux nodes default to the `unless-stopped` [restart policy](../nodes.md#restart-policy), and containerlab keeps the links and the management address of each node in an internal `<node-name>-netns` container. The internal container is only listed by `containerlab inspect --all`, and it is removed together with the node.\n+To support that, SR Linux nodes default to the `unless-stopped` [restart policy](../nodes.md#restart-policy), and containerlab keeps the links and the management address of each node in an internal `<node-name>-netns` container. The internal container is only listed by `containerlab inspect` with the [`--containers`](../../cmd/inspect/index.md#containers) or `--details` flag, and it is removed together with the node.\n \n Use `containerlab stop`, `start` and `restart` to manage the lifecycle of SR Linux nodes instead of restarting the containers with the container runtime directly.\n \n Nodes with a user-defined [`network-mode`](../nodes.md#network-mode) do not use the internal container.\n \ndiff --git a/tests/02-basic-srl/05-inspect-views.clab.yml b/tests/02-basic-srl/05-inspect-views.clab.yml\nnew file Important: `deployFabric` at line 747 calls `n.cpmSlot()` and fails with error if no CPM slot (A or B) exists. So a distributed base node MUST have a CPM slot A or B — deploying without one fails. Therefore the "node vanishes from logical view when no CPM" scenario can only arise if the deploy itself failed (lab not fully deployed), in which case inspect showing nothing for that node matches the pre-existing behavior (base inspect -t listed node containers; with no CPM... hmm, in base, if deploy failed, the containers wouldn't exist anyway). So the missing-CPM edge case is not a realistic regression: deploy would fail first. Good — drop that concern. Actually wait: could a distributed node be deployed with only slot B (no A)? Yes — cpmSlot falls back to B. Then logicalNodeContainers: hasCPMA false → isCPM for "sr-b" = true → shows sr-b. Good, matches the test (lab2 case in the unit test).

Now the `renameDone` question: for distributed card nodes defined as separate nodes (slot env set, no components), those are separate topology nodes registered in c.Nodes with their own names, and they run `DefaultNode` (no netns holder). They don't create component containers. So renameDone only affects... where is renameDone set true? Line 753 after deployFabric — the base node's componentNodes were already created with the calculated names. renameDone=true makes subsequent calcComponentName return the name unchanged (to avoid double-suffixing). This is internal to sros. Not relevant to the inspect heuristics.

But wait — there is one more important scenario: distributed card nodes defined as separate topology nodes. E.g.:
```yaml
nodes:
  sr:
    kind: nokia_srsim
    type: sr-14s
    components: [{slot: A}, {slot: 1}]
  sr-1:
    kind: nokia_srsim
    env: {NOKIA_SROS_SLOT: "1"}
```
Hmm, actually how do separate card nodes work? They are standalone nodes in c.Nodes with a slot env. Their containers get NodeName = their short name (e.g., "sr-1"), no RootNodeName. In the logical view they're included (key.node = "sr-1"). Fine.

But consider a potential collision: a distributed base node "sr" with component "sr-1" AND a separate topology node named... they can't both be named "sr-1" in the topology since component names are derived. Actually a user could define a node named "sr-a" while another node "sr" has CPM A. Then c.Nodes contains both "sr-a" (the standalone node) and the base "sr" with component "sr-a". The label list would contain two containers: one with NodeName="sr-a" RootNodeName="" and one with NodeName="sr-a" RootNodeName="sr". logicalNodeContainers: the standalone one: key={lab,""} → key.node="sr-a" → hasCPMA[{lab,""}]? First pass: for the standalone, key.node="" → skipped in the switch (case key.node == ""). The component: key={lab,"sr"}, NodeName "sr-a" == "sr-a" → hasCPMA[{lab,"sr"}]=true. Second pass: standalone sr-a → included (key.node=="" path). Component sr-a → isCPM true → included. Result: two entries both named "clab-lab-sr-a". In base, the -t view showed both too (ListNodesContainersIgnoreNotFound iterated c.Nodes; the standalone node named sr-a would return its container; the component containers are not in c.Nodes so the base -t didn't show components at all!). Hmm wait — in base, did -t show components? No: base -t listed only containers of c.Nodes nodes (each sros node returns CPM A container for distributed nodes). So base -t showed "sr-a" once (from node "sr" → GetContainers returns the CPM A container). With a separate node named "sr-a", base would show both (the standalone node's container and the CPM A of node sr — names would collide in the runtime? Container names clab-lab-sr-a for both → the runtime wouldn't allow duplicate container names. So this scenario is impossible in practice. Drop it.

Now, the remaining behaviors to verify:

1. `inspect -t` when topology parse fails or lab not deployed: c.Nodes populated from topo; label list by c.Config.Name. If the lab was deployed from the same topo, name matches. But what if the user renamed the lab in the topo after deploying? In base, -t used ListNodesContainersIgnoreNotFound (node-name lookup) — which would find containers by name regardless of the lab-name label? Let me check ListNodesContainersIgnoreNotFound implementation — it iterates c.Nodes and calls node.GetContainers which matches container names by longname. So base -t worked even if the lab-name label mismatched the topo name... Actually if the topo name changed, the longname changes too (clab-<name>-<node>), so node lookup would fail as well. OK.

But a more relevant difference: base -t found containers ONLY via node names. The new -t first lists by lab-name label. 74: 	interfacesC := &cobra.Command{

77: 		Long: "show interfaces and their attributes in a specific deployed lab\n" +
78: 			"reference: https://containerlab.dev/cmd/inspect/interfaces/",

85: 			return clabutils.CheckAndGetRootPrivs()

111: func inspectFn(cobraCmd *cobra.Command, o *Options) error {
112: 	if o.Global.TopologyName == "" && o.Global.TopologyFile == "" && !o.Destroy.All {
113: 		return fmt.Errorf(
114: 			"provide either a lab name (--name) or a topology file path (--topo) or the --all flag",
115: 		)
116: 	}
117: 
118: 	// Format validation (only relevant if --details is NOT used)
119: 	if !o.Inspect.Details &&
120: 		o.Inspect.Format != clabconstants.FormatTable &&
121: 		o.Inspect.Format != clabconstants.FormatJSON &&
122: 		o.Inspect.Format != clabconstants.FormatCSV {
123: 		return fmt.Errorf(
124: 			"output format %q is not supported when --details is not used, use "+
125: 				"'table', 'json' or 'csv'",
126: 			o.Inspect.Format,
127: 		)
128: 	}
129: 	// If --details is used, the format is implicitly JSON.
130: 	if o.Inspect.Details {
131: 		o.Inspect.Format = clabconstants.FormatJSON // Force JSON format if details are requested
132: 	}
133: 
134: 	c, err := clabcore.NewContainerLab(o.ToClabOptions()...)
135: 	if err != nil {
136: 		return err
137: 	}
138: 
139: 	containers, err := listContainers(cobraCmd.Context(), c, o)
140: 	if err != nil {
141: 		return err
142: 	}
143: 
144: 	// Handle empty results
145: 	if len(containers) == 0 {
146: 		switch o.Inspect.Format {
147: 		case clabconstants.FormatJSON:
148: 			fmt.Println("{}")
149: 		case clabconstants.FormatCSV:
150: 			fmt.Println(
151: 				"lab_name,labPath,absLabPath,name,container_id,image,kind,state,status," +
152: 					"ipv4_address,ipv6_address,owner",
153: 			)
154: 		default: // Table format
155: 			log.Info("no containers found")
156: 		}
157: 
158: 		return err
159: 	}
160: 
161: 	// Handle --details (always produces grouped JSON output)
162: 	if o.Inspect.Details {
163: 		return printContainerDetailsJSON(containers)
164: 	}
165: 
166: 	// Handle non-details cases (table or grouped JSON summary)
167: 	err = PrintContainerInspect(containers, o)
168: 
169: 	return err
170: }

172: // listContainers handles listing containers based on different criteria (topology or labels).
173: func listContainers(
174: 	ctx context.Context,
175: 	c *clabcore.CLab,
176: 	o *Options,
177: ) ([]clabruntime.GenericContainer, error) {
178: 	if c.LabRuntime != nil {
179: 		return c.ListLabRuntimeContainers(ctx, o.Destroy.All)
180: 	}
181: 
182: 	var listOptions []clabcore.ListOption
183: 
184: 	switch {
185: 	case o.Global.TopologyFile != "":
186: 		listOptions = append(listOptions, clabcore.WithListLabName(c.Config.Name))
187: 	case o.Global.TopologyName != "":
188: 		listOptions = append(listOptions, clabcore.WithListLabName(o.Global.TopologyName))
189: 	default:
190: 		listOptions = append(listOptions, clabcore.WithListclabLabelExists())
191: 	}
192: 
193: 	containers, err := c.ListContainers(ctx, listOptions...)
194: 	if err != nil {
195: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to list containers based on labels: %s", err)
196: 	}
197: 
198: 	if o.Global.TopologyFile != "" {
199: 		containers = slices.DeleteFunc(containers, func(ctr clabruntime.GenericContainer) bool {
200: 			_, isNode := c.Nodes[ctr.Labels[clabconstants.NodeName]]
201: 			_, isComponent := c.Nodes[ctr.Labels[clabconstants.RootNodeName]]
202: 
203: 			return !isNode && !isComponent
204: 		})
205: 
206: 		// containers that containerlab did not create (ie. ext-container) have no lab labels.
207: 		nodeContainers, err := c.ListNodesContainersIgnoreNotFound(ctx)
208: 		if err != nil {
209: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to list containers based on topology: %s", err)
210: 		}
211: 
212: 		for idx := range nodeContainers {
213: 			if !slices.ContainsFunc(containers, func(ctr clabruntime.GenericContainer) bool {
214: 				return ctr.ID == nodeContainers[idx].ID
215: 			}) {
216: 				containers = append(containers, nodeContainers[idx])
217: 			}
218: 		}
219: 	}
220: 
221: 	// --details always describes every container of a lab.
222: 	if o.Inspect.Containers || o.Inspect.Details {
223: 		return containers, nil
224: 	}
225: 
226: 	return logicalNodeContainers(containers), nil
227: }
228: 
229: // logicalNodeContainers returns a single logical topology node.
230: func logicalNodeContainers(
231: 	containers []clabruntime.GenericContainer,
232: ) []clabruntime.GenericContainer {
233: 	// Node names are unique only within a lab.
234: 	type nodeKey struct{ lab, node string }
235: 
236: 	holders := make(map[nodeKey]*clabruntime.GenericContainer)
237: 	hasCPMA := make(map[nodeKey]bool)
238: 
239: 	for idx := range containers {
240: 		l := containers[idx].Labels
241: 		key := nodeKey{l[clabconstants.Containerlab], l[clabconstants.RootNodeName]}
242: 
243: 		switch {
244: 		case key.node == "":
245: 		case l[clabconstants.InternalNode] == "true":
246: 			holders[key] = &containers[idx]
247: 		case l[clabconstants.NodeName] == key.node+"-a":
248: 			hasCPMA[key] = true
249: 		}
250: 	}
251: 
252: 	result := make([]clabruntime.GenericContainer, 0, len(containers))
253: 
254: 	for idx := range containers {
255: 		ctr := containers[idx]
256: 		name := ctr.Labels[clabconstants.NodeName]
257: 		key := nodeKey{
258: 			ctr.Labels[clabconstants.Containerlab],
259: 			ctr.Labels[clabconstants.RootNodeName],
260: 		}
261: 
262: 		// Components are named <root node>-<lowercase slot>.
263: 		isCPM := name == key.node+"-a" || (name == key.node+"-b" && !hasCPMA[key])
264: 		if ctr.Labels[clabconstants.ToolType] != "" ||
265: 			ctr.Labels[clabconstants.InternalNode] == "true" || (key.node != "" && !isCPM) {
266: 			continue
267: 		}
268: 
269: 		if key.node == "" {
270: 			key.node = name
271: 		}
272: 
273: 		if holder := holders[key]; holder != nil {
274: 			ctr.NetworkName = holder.NetworkName
275: 			ctr.NetworkSettings = holder.NetworkSettings
276: 			ctr.Ports = holder.Ports
277: 		}
278: 
279: 		result = append(result, ctr)
280: 	}
281: 
282: 	return result
283: }

285: func toTableData(contDetails []clabtypes.ContainerDetails, o *Options) []tableWriter.Row {
286: 	tabData := make([]tableWriter.Row, 0, len(contDetails))
287: 
288: 	for i := range contDetails {
289: 		d := &contDetails[i]
290: 		tabRow := tableWriter.Row{}
291: 
292: 		if o.Destroy.All {
293: 			tabRow = append(tabRow, d.LabPath, d.LabName)
294: 		}
295: 
296: 		if o.Inspect.Wide {
297: 			tabRow = append(tabRow, d.Owner)
298: 		}
299: 
300: 		// we do not want to print status other than health in the table view
301: 		if !strings.Contains(d.Status, "health") {
302: 			d.Status = ""
303: 		} else {
304: 			d.Status = fmt.Sprintf("(%s)", d.Status)
305: 		}
306: 
307: 		// Common fields
308: 		if o.Inspect.Wide {
309: 			// Print all fields on one line, no newlines
310: 			tabRow = append(tabRow,
311: 				d.Name,
312: 				fmt.Sprintf("%s %s", d.Kind, d.Image),
313: 				fmt.Sprintf("%s %s", d.State, d.Status),
314: 				fmt.Sprintf("%s %s",
315: 					ipWithoutPrefix(d.IPv4Address),
316: 					ipWithoutPrefix(d.IPv6Address)))
317: 		} else {
318: 			tabRow = append(tabRow,
319: 				d.Name,
320: 				fmt.Sprintf("%s\n%s", d.Kind, d.Image),
321: 				fmt.Sprintf("%s\n%s", d.State, d.Status),
322: 				fmt.Sprintf("%s\n%s",
323: 					ipWithoutPrefix(d.IPv4Address),
324: 					ipWithoutPrefix(d.IPv6Address)))
325: 		}
326: 
327: 		tabData = append(tabData, tabRow)
328: 	}
329: 
330: 	return tabData
331: }

333: // getShortestTopologyPath calculates the relative path to the provided topology file from
334: // the current working directory and returns it if it is shorted than the absolute path p.
335: func getShortestTopologyPath(p string) (string, error) {
336: 	if p == "" {
337: 		return "", nil
338: 	}
339: 	if strings.Contains(p, "://") {
340: 		return p, nil
341: 	}
342: 
343: 	// get topo file path relative of the cwd
344: 	cwd, err := os.Getwd()
345: 	if err != nil {
346: 		return "", err
347: 	}
348: 
349: 	relPath, err := filepath.Rel(cwd, p)
350: 	if err != nil {
351: 		return "", err
352: 	}
353: 
354: 	if len(relPath) < len(p) {
355: 		return relPath, nil
356: 	}
357: 
358: 	return p, nil
359: }

361: // printContainerDetailsJSON handles the detailed JSON output of containers grouped by lab name.
362: func printContainerDetailsJSON(containers []clabruntime.GenericContainer) error {
363: 	groupedDetails := make(map[string][]clabruntime.GenericContainer)
364: 	// Sort containers first by lab name, then by container name for consistent output
365: 	sort.Slice(containers, func(i, j int) bool {
366: 		labNameI := containers[i].Labels[clabconstants.Containerlab]
367: 		labNameJ := containers[j].Labels[clabconstants.Containerlab]
368: 
369: 		if labNameI == labNameJ {
370: 			// Use the first name if available
371: 			nameI := ""
372: 			if len(containers[i].Names) > 0 {
373: 				nameI = containers[i].Names[0]
374: 			}
375: 
376: 			nameJ := ""
377: 			if len(containers[j].Names) > 0 {
378: 				nameJ = containers[j].Names[0]
379: 			}
380: 
381: 			return nameI < nameJ
382: 		}
383: 
384: 		return labNameI < labNameJ
385: 	})
386: 
387: 	// Group the sorted containers
388: 	for idx := range containers {
389: 		labName := containers[idx].Labels[clabconstants.Containerlab]
390: 		// Ensure labName exists, default to a placeholder if missing
391: 		// (shouldn't happen with filters)
392: 		if labName == "" {
393: 			labName = "_unknown_lab_"
394: 		}
395: 
396: 		groupedDetails[labName] = append(groupedDetails[labName], containers[idx])
397: 	}
398: 
399: 	b, err := json.MarshalIndent(groupedDetails, "", "  ")
400: 	if err != nil {
401: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal grouped container details: %v", err)
402: 	}
403: 
404: 	fmt.Println(string(b))
405: 
406: 	return nil
407: }

409: func printContainerInspectJSON(contDetails []clabtypes.ContainerDetails) error {
410: 	// Group summary results by LabName
411: 	// Use a map where keys are lab names and values are slices of container details
412: 	groupedLabs := make(map[string][]clabtypes.ContainerDetails)
413: 
414: 	for idx := range contDetails {
415: 		labName := contDetails[idx].LabName
416: 		if labName == "" {
417: 			labName = "_unknown_lab_" // Should not happen if filters work correctly
418: 		}
419: 		// Assign the *entire* ContainerDetails struct (including AbsLabPath)
420: 		groupedLabs[labName] = append(groupedLabs[labName], contDetails[idx])
421: 	}
422: 
423: 	b, err := json.MarshalIndent(groupedLabs, "", "  ")
424: 	if err != nil {
425: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal grouped container summary: %v", err)
426: 	}
427: 
428: 	fmt.Println(string(b))
429: 
430: 	return nil
431: }

433: func printContainerInspectTable(contDetails []clabtypes.ContainerDetails, o *Options) {
434: 	// Generate and render table using the summary data (which uses relative LabPath)
435: 	tabData := toTableData(contDetails, o)
436: 	table := tableWriter.NewWriter()
437: 	table.SetOutputMirror(os.Stdout)
438: 	table.SetStyle(tableWriter.StyleRounded)
439: 	table.Style().Format.Header = text.FormatTitle
440: 	table.Style().Format.HeaderAlign = text.AlignCenter
441: 	table.Style().Options.SeparateRows = true
442: 	table.Style().Color = tableWriter.ColorOptions{
443: 		Header: text.Colors{text.Bold},
444: 	}
445: 
446: 	headerBase := tableWriter.Row{"Name", "Kind/Image", "State", "IPv4/6 Address"}
447: 	if o.Inspect.Wide {
448: 		headerBase = slices.Insert(headerBase, 0, "Owner")
449: 	}
450: 
451: 	var header tableWriter.Row
452: 
453: 	var colConfigs []tableWriter.ColumnConfig
454: 
455: 	// Lab-level columns (Topology, Lab Name, Owner) AutoMerge across nodes of the same lab.
456: 	if o.Destroy.All {
457: 		header = append(tableWriter.Row{"Topology", "Lab Name"}, headerBase...)
458: 		colConfigs = append(
459: 			colConfigs,
460: 			tableWriter.ColumnConfig{
461: 				Number:    1,
462: 				AutoMerge: true, VAlign: text.VAlignMiddle,
463: 			},
464: 			tableWriter.ColumnConfig{
465: 				Number:    2, //nolint: mnd
466: 				AutoMerge: true, VAlign: text.VAlignMiddle,
467: 			},
468: 		)
469: 		if o.Inspect.Wide {
470: 			colConfigs = append(colConfigs, tableWriter.ColumnConfig{
471: 				Number:    3, //nolint: mnd
472: 				AutoMerge: true, VAlign: text.VAlignMiddle,
473: 			})
474: 		}
475: 	} else {
476: 		header = headerBase
477: 
478: 		colConfigs = append(colConfigs, tableWriter.ColumnConfig{
479: 			Number:    1,
480: 			AutoMerge: true, VAlign: text.VAlignMiddle,
481: 		})
482: 	}
483: 
484: 	table.AppendHeader(header)
485: 
486: 	if len(colConfigs) > 0 {
487: 		table.SetColumnConfigs(colConfigs)
488: 	}
489: 
490: 	table.AppendRows(tabData)
491: 	table.Render()
492: }

516: // PrintContainerInspect handles non-details output (table or grouped JSON summary).
517: func PrintContainerInspect(containers []clabruntime.GenericContainer, o *Options) error {
518: 	contDetails := make([]clabtypes.ContainerDetails, 0, len(containers))
519: 
520: 	// Gather summary details of each container
521: 	for idx := range containers {
522: 		absPath := containers[idx].Labels[clabconstants.TopoFile]
523: 
524: 		shortPath, err := getShortestTopologyPath(absPath)
525: 		if err != nil {
526: 			log.Warnf(
527: 				"failed to get relative topology path for container %s: %v, using raw path %q",
528: 				containers[idx].Names[0],
529: 				err,
530: 				absPath,
531: 			)
532: 
533: 			shortPath = absPath // Use raw path as fallback for display
534: 		}
535: 
536: 		status := parseStatus(containers[idx].Status)
537: 
538: 		cdet := clabtypes.ContainerDetails{
539: 			LabName:     containers[idx].Labels[clabconstants.Containerlab],
540: 			LabPath:     shortPath, // Relative or shortest path for table view
541: 			AbsLabPath:  absPath,   // Absolute path for JSON view
542: 			Image:       containers[idx].Image,
543: 			State:       containers[idx].State,
544: 			Status:      status,
545: 			IPv4Address: containers[idx].GetContainerIPv4(),
546: 			IPv6Address: containers[idx].GetContainerIPv6(),
547: 			ContainerID: containers[idx].ShortID,
548: 			// Only lab runtimes set the workload; it adds namespace, pod, container, node_uid,
549: 			// exposed_ports and load_balancer_address to the JSON output.
550: 			LabRuntimeWorkload: containers[idx].Workload,
551: 		}
552: 
553: 		if len(containers[idx].Names) > 0 {
554: 			cdet.Name = containers[idx].Names[0]
555: 		}
556: 
557: 		if group, ok := containers[idx].Labels[clabconstants.NodeGroup]; ok {
558: 			cdet.Group = group
559: 		}
560: 
561: 		if kind, ok := containers[idx].Labels[clabconstants.NodeKind]; ok {
562: 			cdet.Kind = kind
563: 		}
564: 
565: 		if owner, ok := containers[idx].Labels[clabconstants.Owner]; ok {
566: 			cdet.Owner = owner
567: 		}
568: 
569: 		contDetails = append(contDetails, cdet)
570: 	}
571: 
572: 	// Sort summary details by lab name, then container name
573: 	sort.Slice(contDetails, func(i, j int) bool {
574: 		if contDetails[i].LabName == contDetails[j].LabName {
575: 			return contDetails[i].Name < contDetails[j].Name
576: 		}
577: 
578: 		return contDetails[i].LabName < contDetails[j].LabName
579: 	})
580: 
581: 	switch o.Inspect.Format {
582: 	case clabconstants.FormatJSON:
583: 		err := printContainerInspectJSON(contDetails)
584: 		if err != nil {
585: 			return err
586: 		}
587: 	case "table":
588: 		printContainerInspectTable(contDetails, o)
589: 	case "csv":
590: 		printContainerInspectCSV(contDetails)
591: 	default:
592: 		return fmt.Errorf("internal error: unhandled format %q", o.Inspect.Format)
593: 	}
594: 
595: 	return nil
596: }
597: 
598: // parseStatus extracts a simpler status string, focusing on health states.
599: func parseStatus(status string) string {
600: 	switch {
601: 	case strings.Contains(status, "unhealthy"):
602: 		return "unhealthy"
603: 	case strings.Contains(status, "health: starting"):
604: 		return "health: starting"
605: 	case strings.Contains(status, "healthy"):
606: 		return "healthy"
607: 	default:
608: 		// Return original status if no specific health info found
609: 		return status
610: 	}
611: }
612: 
613: // ipWithoutPrefix removes the CIDR prefix length from an IP address string.
614: // Returns "N/A" if input contains "N/A".
615: // Returns original string if it doesn't contain exactly one "/".
616: func ipWithoutPrefix(ip string) string {
617: 	if strings.Contains(ip, clabconstants.NotApplicable) {
618: 		return ip
619: 	}
620: 
621: 	ipParts := strings.Split(ip, "/")
622: 	if len(ipParts) != 2 { //nolint: mnd
623: 		return ip // Return original if not in expected format "address/prefix"
624: 	}
625: 
626: 	return ipParts[0]
627: }

So their containers have NodeName = sidecar name ∈ c.Nodes, ToolType="tailscale", InternalNode="true". In logicalNodeContainers they're skipped (ToolType + InternalNode). Consistent with base behavior (InternalNode filtered). Good.

The tailscale proxy: created via createTailscaleProxy with addDefaultLabels → NodeName = ProxyName shortname. Is the proxy in c.Nodes? It's created post-deploy (tool), probably not in c.Nodes. Its labels: ToolType="tailscale", InternalNode="true", NodeName="proxy"(?). In logicalNodeContainers → skipped (ToolType). In base --all: it had InternalNode → also filtered when !--all... base `inspect --all`: o.Destroy.All=true → filter skipped → proxy SHOWN in base --all.
