5: 
6: # Inspect command
7: 
8: ### Description
9: 
10: The `inspect` command provides the information about the deployed labs.
11: 
12: /// note | Clabernetes runtime
13: With `--runtime c9s`, `inspect` reads Clabernetes `Topology` resources and their related kubernetes objects instead of local Docker containers. `inspect --all` lists c9s topologies across all namespaces, or in the `--namespace` override. The JSON output uses `<namespace>/<lab>/<node>` as `container_id` and adds the `namespace`, `pod`, `container`, `node_uid`, `exposed_ports` and `load_balancer_address` fields. See [Containerlab runtime](../../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#inspect) for details.
14: ///
15: 
16: ### Usage
17: 
18: `containerlab [global-flags] inspect [local-flags]`
19: 
20: ### Flags
21: 
22: #### all
23: 
24: With the local `--all` flag it's possible to list all deployed labs in a single table. The output will also show the relative path to the topology file that was used to spawn this lab.
25: 
26: The lab name and path values will be set for the first node of such lab, to reduce the clutter. Refer to the [examples](#examples) section for more details.
27: 
28: #### topology | name
29: 
30: With the global `--topo | -t` flag a user sets the path to the topology definition file that will be used to spin up a lab.
31: 
32: When the topology path refers to a directory, containerlab will look for a file with `.clab.yml` extension in that directory and use it as a topology definition file.
33: 
34: When the topology file flag is omitted, containerlab will try to find the matching file name by looking at the current working directory.
35: 
36: If more than one file is found for directory-based path or when the flag is omitted entirely, containerlab will fail with an error.
37: 
38: #### format
39: 
40: The local `--format` flag enables different output stylings. By default the table view will be used.
41: 
42: Available format options are:
43: 
44: - `json` - outputs the inspect data in JSON format
45: - `csv` - outputs the inspect data as comma-separated values.
46: 
47: The data is provided in the context of a container that belongs to a containerlab lab. Both output formats will provide you with the following data:
48: 
49: | Field          | Description                                                                                              |
50: |----------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
51: | `lab_name`     | The name of the lab.                                                                                     |
52: | `labPath`      | The relative path to the lab topology file.                                                              |
53: | `absLabPath`   | The absolute path to the lab topology file.                                                              |
54: | `name`         | The name of the container.                                                                               |
55: | `container_id` | The unique ID of the container.                                                                          |
56: | `image`        | The container's [image](../../manual/nodes.md#image).                                                    |
57: | `kind`         | The container's [kind](../../manual/nodes.md#kind).                                                      |
58: | `state`        | The container's state. ie. `created`, `restarting`, `running`, `removing`, `paused`, `exited`, or `dead` |
59: | `status`       | The health status of the container. ie `starting`, `unhealthy`, `up` or `exited`.                        |
60: | `ipv4_address` | The [IPv4 management address](../../manual/nodes.md#mgmt-ipv4) of the container.                            |
61: | `ipv6_address` | The [IPv6 management address](../../manual/nodes.md#mgmt-ipv6) of the container.                            |
62: | `owner`        | The [owner](../deploy.md#owner) of the lab.                                                                 |
63: 
64: #### details
65: 
66: The `inspect` command produces a brief summary about the running lab components. It is also possible to get a full view on the running containers by adding `--details` flag.
67: 
68: With this flag inspect command will output every bit of information about the running containers. This is what `docker inspect` command provides.
69: 
70: #### containers
71: 
72: By default `inspect` shows one entry per topology node.
73: 
74: Nodes that consist of several containers (ie. distributed SR-SIM) are represented by a single node that carries the management addresses of the node.
75: 
76: The local flag `--containers` will list every container of a lab rather than just the logical nodes.
77: 
78: When the lab is selected with the `--topo` flag, only the containers of the nodes defined in that topology file are listed.
79: 
80: #### wide
81: 
82: The local `-w | --wide` flag adds all available columns to the `inspect` output table.
83: 
84: ### Examples
85: 
86: #### List all running labs on the host
87: 
88: ```bash
89: ❯ containerlab inspect --all
90: +---+------------+----------+-----------------+--------------+--------------------+------+-------+---------+----------------+----------------------+
91: | # | Topo Path  | Lab Name |      Name       | Container ID |       Image        | Kind | Group |  State  |  IPv4 Address  |     IPv6 Address     |
92: +---+------------+----------+-----------------+--------------+--------------------+------+-------+---------+----------------+----------------------+
93: | 1 | newlab.yml | newlab   | clab-newlab-n1  | 3c8262034088 | srlinux:20.6.3-145 | srl  |       | running | 172.20.20.4/24 | 3fff:172:20:20::4/80 |
94: | 2 |            |          | clab-newlab-n2  | 79c562b71997 | srlinux:20.6.3-145 | srl  |       | running | 172.20.20.5/24 | 3fff:172:20:20::5/80 |
95: | 3 | srl02.yml  | srl01    | clab-srl01-srl  | 13c9e7543771 | srlinux:20.6.3-145 | srl  |       | running | 172.20.20.2/24 | 3fff:172:20:20::2/80 |
96: | 4 |            |          | clab-srl01-srl2 | 8cfca93b7b6f | srlinux:20.6.3-145 | srl  |       | running | 172.20.20.3/24 | 3fff:172:20:20::3/80 |
97: +---+------------+----------+-----------------+--------------+--------------------+------+-------+---------+----------------+----------------------+
98: ```
99: 
100: #### Provide information about a specific running lab by its name
101: 
102: Provide information about the running lab named `srlceos01`

110: | 2 | clab-srlceos01-srl  | 82e9aa3c7e6b | srlinux | srl  |       | running | 172.20.20.3/24 | 3fff:172:20:20::3/80 |
111: +---+---------------------+--------------+---------+------+-------+---------+----------------+----------------------+

124: +---+-----------------+--------------+-----------------------+------+---------+----------------+----------------------+

126: 
127: #### Provide owner information of running labs
128: 
129: An owner is a linux user that started the lab. When `sudo` is used, the original user is displayed as the owner.

        "text": "---\ntags:\n  - Command\n---\n\n# Inspect command\n\n### Description\n\nThe `inspect` command provides the information about the deployed labs.\n\n/// note | Clabernetes runtime\nWith `--runtime c9s`, `inspect` reads Clabernetes `Topology` resources and their related kubernetes objects instead of local Docker containers. `inspect --all` lists c9s topologies across all namespaces, or in the `--namespace` override. The JSON output uses `<namespace>/<lab>/<node>` as `container_id` and adds the `namespace`, `pod`, `container`, `node_uid`, `exposed_ports` and `load_balancer_address` fields. See [Containerlab runtime](../../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#inspect) for details.\n///\n\n### Usage\n\n`containerlab [global-flags] inspect [local-flags]`\n\n### Flags\n\n#### all\n\nWith the local `--all` flag it's possible to list all deployed labs in a single table. The output will also show the relative path to the topology file that was used to spawn this lab.\n\nThe lab name and path values will be set for the first node of such lab, to reduce the clutter. Refer to the [examples](#examples) section for more details.\n\n#### topology | name\n\nWith the global `--topo | -t` flag a user sets the path to the topology definition file that will be used to spin up a lab.\n\nWhen the topology path refers to a directory, containerlab will look for a file with `.clab.yml` extension in that directory and use it as a topology definition file.\n\nWhen the topology file flag is omitted, containerlab will try to find the matching file name by looking at the current working directory.\n\nIf more than one file is found for directory-based path or when the flag is omitted entirely, containerlab will fail with an error.\n\n#### format\n\nThe local `--format` flag enables different output stylings. By default the table view will be used.\n\nAvailable format options are:\n\n- `json` - outputs the inspect data in JSON format\n- `csv` - outputs the inspect data as comma-separated values.\n\nThe data is provided in the context of a container that belongs to a containerlab lab. Both output formats will provide you with the following data:\n\n| Field          | Description                                                                                              |\n|----------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `lab_name`     | The name of the lab.                                                                                     |\n| `labPath`      | The relative path to the lab topology file.                                                              |\n| `absLabPath`   | The absolute path to the lab topology file.                                                              |\n| `name`         | The name of the container.                                                                               |\n| `container_id` | The unique ID of the container.                                                                          |\n| `image`        | The container's [image](../../manual/nodes.md#image).                                                    |\n| `kind`         | The container's [kind](../../manual/nodes.md#kind).                                                      |\n| `state`        | The container's state. ie. `created`, `restarting`, `running`, `removing`, `paused`, `exited`, or `dead` |\n| `status`       | The health status of the container. ie `starting`, `unhealthy`, `up` or `exited`.                        |\n| `ipv4_address` | The [IPv4 management address](../../manual/nodes.md#mgmt-ipv4) of the container.                            |\n| `ipv6_address` | The [IPv6 management address](../../manual/nodes.md#mgmt-ipv6) of the container.                            |\n| `owner`        | The [owner](../deploy.md#owner) of the lab.                                                                 |\n\n#### details\n\nThe `inspect` command produces a brief summary about the running lab components. It is also possible to get a full view on the running containers by adding `--details` flag.\n\nWith this flag inspect command will output every bit of information about the running containers. This is what `docker inspect` command provides.\n\n#### containers\n\nBy default `inspect` shows one entry per topology node.\n\nNodes that consist of several containers (ie. distributed SR-SIM) are represented by a single node that carries the management addresses of the node.\n\nThe local flag `--containers` will list every container of a lab rather than just the logical nodes.\n\nWhen the lab is selected with the `--topo` flag, only the containers of the nodes defined in that topology file are listed.\n\n#### wide\n\nThe local `-w | --wide` flag adds all available columns to the `inspect` output table.\n\n### Examples\n\n#### List all running labs on the host\n\n```bash\n❯ containerlab inspect --all\n+---+------------+----------+-----------------+--------------+--------------------+------+-------+---------+----------------+----------------------+\n| # | Topo Path  | Lab Name |      Name       | Container ID |       Image        | Kind | Group |  State  |  IPv4 Address  |     IPv6 Address     |\n+---+------------+----------+-----------------+--------------+--------------------+------+-------+---------+----------------+----------------------+\n| 1 | newlab.yml | newlab   | clab-newlab-n1  | 3c8262034088 | srlinux:20.6.3-145 | srl  |       | running | 172.20.20.4/24 | 3fff:172:20:20::4/80 |\n| 2 |            |          | clab-newlab-n2  | 79c562b71997 | srlinux:20.6.3-145 | srl  |       | running | 172.20.20.5/24 | 3fff:172:20:20::5/80 |\n| 3 | srl02.yml  | srl01    | clab-srl01-srl  | 13c9e7543771 | srlinux:20.6.3-145 | srl  |       | running | 172.20.20.2/24 | 3fff:172:20:20::2/80 |\n| 4 |            |          | clab-srl01-srl2 | 8cfca93b7b6f | srlinux:20.6.3-145 | srl  |       | running | 172.20.20.3/24 | 3fff:172:20:20::3/80 |\n+---+------------+----------+-----------------+--------------+--------------------+------+-------+---------+----------------+----------------------+\n```\n\n#### Provide information about a specific running lab by its name\n\nProvide information about the running lab named `srlceos01`\n\n```bash\n❯ containerlab inspect --name srlceos01\n+---+---------------------+--------------+---------+------+-------+---------+----------------+----------------------+\n| # |        Name         | Container ID |  Image  | Kind | Group |  State  |  IPv4 Address  |     IPv6 Address     |\n+---+---------------------+--------------+---------+------+-------+---------+----------------+----------------------+\n| 1 | clab-srlceos01-ceos | 90bebb1e2c5f | ceos    | ceos |       | running | 172.20.20.4/24 | 3fff:172:20:20::4/80 |\n| 2 | clab-srlceos01-srl  | 82e9aa3c7e6b | srlinux | srl  |       | running | 172.20.20.3/24 | 3fff:172:20:20::3/80 |\n+---+---------------------+--------------+---------+------+-------+---------+----------------+----------------------+\n```\n\n#### Provide information about a specific running lab by its topology file\n\n```bash\n❯ clab inspect -t srl02.clab.yml\nINFO[0000] Parsing & checking topology file: srl02.clab.yml\n+---+-----------------+--------------+-----------------------+------+---------+----------------+----------------------+\n| # |      Name       | Container ID |         Image         | Kind |  State  |  IPv4 Address  |     IPv6 Address     |\n+---+-----------------+--------------+-----------------------+------+---------+----------------+----------------------+\n| 1 | clab-srl02-srl1 | 7a7c101be7d8 | ghcr.io/nokia/srlinux | srl  | running | 172.20.20.4/24 | 3fff:172:20:20::4/64 |\n| 2 | clab-srl02-srl2 | 5e3737621753 | ghcr.io/nokia/srlinux | srl  | running | 172.20.20.5/24 | 3fff:172:20:20::5/64 |\n+---+-----------------+--------------+-----------------------+------+---------+----------------+----------------------+\n```\n\n#### Provide owner information of running labs\n\nAn owner is a linux user that started the lab. When `sudo` is used, the original user is displayed as the owner.\n\n```bash\nclab inspect --all |\n+---+-----------------------------------+----------+-------+-----------------+--------------+-----------------------+---------------+---------+----------------+----------------------+\n| 1 | lab-examples/srl02/srl02.clab.yml | srl02    | user2 | clab-srl02-srl1 | ba7e807235b6 | ghcr.io/nokia/srlinux | nokia_srlinux | running | 172.20.20.4/24 | 3fff:172:20:20::4/64 |\n| 3 | <content>
1: name: srlinux-tests
2: 
3: "on":
4:   workflow_call:
5:     inputs:
6:       py_ver:
7:         required: true
8:         type: string
9:       uv_ver:
10:         required: true
11:         type: string
12:       runtime:
13:         type: string
14:         default: "docker"
15: 
16: jobs:
17:   srlinux-tests:
18:     runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
19:     strategy:
20:       matrix:
21:         test-suite:
22:           - "01*.robot"
23:           - "03*.robot"
24:           - "04*.robot"
25:           - "05*.robot"
26:     # allow podman job to fail, since it started to fail on github actions
27:     continue-on-error: ${{ inputs.runtime == 'podman' }}
28:     steps:
29:       - name: Checkout
30:         uses: actions/checkout@v7
31:         with:
32:           fetch-depth: 0
33: 
34:       - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
35:         with:
36:           name: containerlab-tests
37: 
38:       - name: Move containerlab to usr/bin
39:         run: sudo mv ./containerlab /usr/bin/containerlab && sudo chown root:root /usr/bin/containerlab && sudo chmod 4755 /usr/bin/containerlab
40: 
41:       - name: Setup Podman
42:         if: inputs.runtime == 'podman'
43:         # check http://download.opensuse.org/repositories/devel:/kubic:/libcontainers:/unstable/xUbuntu_22.04/amd64/
44:         # for available podman releases
45:         run: sudo bash ./.github/workflows/install-podman.sh
46: 
47:       - name: Install uv
48:         uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7
49:         with:
50:           # Install a specific version of uv.
51:           version: ${{ inputs.uv_ver }}
52:           enable-cache: true
53: 
54:       - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
55:         with:
56:           # cache: pip
57:           # cache-dependency-path: "tests/requirements.txt"
58:           python-version-file: "pyproject.toml"
59: 
60:       - name: Install the project
61:         run: uv sync --all-extras --dev
62: 
63:       # - name: setup tmate session
64:       #   uses: mxschmitt/action-tmate@v3
65: 
66:       - name: Activate virtualenv
67:         run: |
68:           . .venv/bin/activate
69:           echo PATH=$PATH >> $GITHUB_ENV
70: 
71:       - name: Sanitize test-suite name
72:         run: echo "TEST_SUITE=$(echo ${{ matrix.test-suite }} | tr -d '*')" >> $GITHUB_ENV
73: 
74:       - name: Run srlinux tests
75:         run: |
76:           bash ./tests/rf-run.sh ${{ inputs.runtime }} ./tests/02-basic-srl/${{ matrix.test-suite }}
77: 
78:       # upload test reports as a zip file
79:       - name: Upload test logs
80:         uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
81:         if: always()
82:         with:
83:           name: 02-basic-srl-log-${{ env.TEST_SUITE }}-${{ inputs.runtime }}
84:           path: ./tests/out/*.html
85: 
86:       # upload coverage report from unit tests, as they are then
87:       # merged with e2e tests coverage
88:       - name: Upload coverage
89:         uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
90:         if: always()
91:         with:
92:           name: coverage-srlinux-tests-${{ env.TEST_SUITE }}-${{ inputs.runtime }}
93:           path: /tmp/clab-tests/coverage/*
94:           retention-days: 7

(End of file - total 94 lines)
</content>

For the srsim case (`sr-a` + `sr-netns`): the label-list `sr-a` container has no IP (netns-attached), the node-forge sr-a entry (same ID) is discarded by dedup, and the holder's settings are copied ✓. This is exactly what the test checks.

Now — **the `-t` merge dedup keeps the FIRST occurrence. The label list order comes from the runtime (docker order by created time). The node-forge order is by node iteration. For a normal linux node, the label-list entry and the forge entry are the same container with possibly different data (e.g. `Status` field, `State`). Which is authoritative? Both come from the runtime. Fine.

Hmm, but one case: **the sros node forge applies `distNodeMgmtIPs`** — overridden NetworkSettings on the CPM A container. If the actual runtime state differs (e.g., CPM A killed → fallback holder), the dedup keeps the label-list entry. Fine.

Now — **one more scenario for `Inspect Should List` with `--name ${lab-name}`: label list by lab name → same as --all within this lab ✓.**

where `isComponent = c.Nodes[ctr.Labels[RootNodeName]]`. For the netns holder, RootNodeName = the srl node's ShortName ∈ c.Nodes → kept. For srsim components, RootNodeName ∈ c.Nodes → kept. Do c9s workloads carry InternalNode? Let me check ListLabRuntimeContainers.

c9s containers never carry `InternalNode` or `ToolType` labels (only Containerlab, NodeName, LongName, TopoFile, NodeKind). Also, c9s lists only Topology nodes (no internal containers). So the removal of the PrintContainerInspect internal filter doesn't regress c9s. Good.

Documented in the docs (`#### containers`: "By default inspect shows one entry per topology node"). I don't think this is a defect. Skip or coverage note.

**F3: The `-t` path performs two list operations and an O(n²) merge.** Minor perf, n bounded by lab size. Not worth a finding. Skip.

**F4: `logicalNodeContainers` name-suffix heuristic vs. `NodeType`/component labels.** The `-a`/`-b` suffix heuristic is the core of the feature and is well tested. A real edge: a component slot named "a" or "b" lowercase? calcComponentName lowercases the slot → "sr-a"/"sr-b" — handled. What about integrated SROS redundant components (isIntegratedSrosNodeType + redundant components → distributed base)? Components there are CPM slots A/B too. OK.

Hmm wait — actually there IS one edge worth checking: **integrated SROS node types with redundant components — is the component slot list required to include A?** For integrated types, `integratedSrosSlotAllowed(nodeType, slot)` — line 261. If an integrated node has components [{slot: B}, {slot: C}]? isRedundantIntegratedSrosComponents checks... line 249. Let me look at it — if components are "redundant" (more than default?), isDistributedBaseNode → true. Then deployFabric → cpmSlot() errors if no A/B slot → deploy fails. So again, deploy fails first. Fine.

**F5: A REAL potential issue — `hasCPMA` detection when the CPM A container is a tool? No. When CPM A container has `InternalNode`? No. Fine.

**F7: A REAL issue candidate — `inspect -t` behavior change: containers belonging to the lab but NOT in c.Nodes and not components are now EXCLUDED from `-t` output. In base, `-t` used ListNodesContainersIgnoreNotFound — which ALSO only returned containers of c.Nodes nodes. So no change. ✓

**F8: REAL issue candidate — the -t label list uses `c.Config.Name` but the -t path in base ALSO included containers whose TopoFile label matched but lab name label mismatched? No — base -t used node name lookups only.

Hmm, wait. Actually there IS one real behavioral difference in the -t path worth flagging: **base `-t` looked up containers by NODE (GetContainers per node), which for the srl kind returns the srl container with the holder's network settings, and for distributed sros returns CPM A with distNodeMgmtIPs. Head `-t` first lists by the LAB NAME label and then merges. If a node's container is running but its lab-name label was overwritten (e.g., `tools netem` or manual relabel)? Not realistic.

Another real difference: **base `-t` matched containers BY NAME (longname = clab-<lab>-<node>). Head `-t` matches by the `containerlab` LABEL. For an ext-container node, the ext-container has NO clab label but IS returned by GetContainers (found by name) → merged in ✓.

But here's one: **the `containerlab` label is set to `c.Config.Name` at config time; if the lab was deployed BEFORE with a different config name (e.g. the dir was renamed after deploy), `-t` now finds nothing (label mismatch) while base found containers by name (name also mismatched). Equivalent. Fine.

## Code Review: logical `inspect` views for SR Linux / SR-SIM components

**Scope**: 15 changed paths reviewed across head (`fa10709`) and base (`58ef691`). Source-only review; no tests or commands were executed.

### Summary Table

| Priority | Finding | Location |
|----------|---------|----------|
| P4 | Unnecessary `slices.Clone` before `slices.DeleteFunc` in `deployFn` | [cmd/deploy.go#L336-L341](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fa1070982d24f060198ba82bebd9dd74d4048e33/cmd/deploy.go#L336-L341) |

### Finding Details

#### P4 — Unnecessary `slices.Clone` before `slices.DeleteFunc` in `deployFn`

**Location**: [`cmd/deploy.go` lines 336–343](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fa1070982d24f060198ba82bebd9dd74d4048e33/cmd/deploy.go#L336-L343) (head)

**Problem**: The PR moved the internal-container filter out of `PrintContainerInspect` into `deployFn` and wrapped it with `slices.Clone(result.Containers)`. The clone exists to protect `result.Containers` from `slices.DeleteFunc` mutation, but `result.Containers` is never read again: `deployFn` returns immediately after `PrintContainerInspect(containers, o)` on line 343. All other consumers (`result.Apply`, the version check) operate on different fields of the result.

**Trigger**: Every `deploy`/`redeploy` invocation that prints the container summary.

**Impact**: One avoidable slice copy per deploy (negligible at realistic lab sizes) and, more importantly, a maintenance question: a reader may assume `result.Containers` is needed in its unfiltered form elsewhere. This is the only reason the clone exists, and it does not.

**Correction**: Drop `slices.Clone` and apply `slices.DeleteFunc` directly to `result.Containers`:

```go
containers := slices.DeleteFunc(result.Containers, func(ctr clabruntime.GenericContainer) bool {
    return ctr.Labels[clabconstants.InternalNode] == "true"
})
```

If defensive copying is preferred, a brief comment naming the protected caller would serve the same clarity purpose. Optional; either form is acceptable.

### Behavior changes verified as intentional and documented

- **Default inspect view** now collapses SR Linux netns holders and SR-SIM components/CPMs into one entry per topology node (keyed by lab + root node name, CPM A preferred with CPM B shown when A is absent). The `#### containers` section in `docs/cmd/inspect/index.md` documents this, and the `--containers` flag help text covers the raw view.
- **Tool containers** (`sshx`, `gotty`, `api-server`) carry `NodeType: tool` / `ToolType` labels and no topology-node `NodeName`, so they are hidden from the default view and shown with `--containers`/`--details`. With `-t`, they are also excluded from `--containers` because the label-list filter keeps only containers whose `NodeName` or `RootNodeName` belongs to the topology — consistent with the documented "-t lists only containers of nodes defined in the topology file" semantics.
- **Clabernetes path** bypasses `logicalNodeContainers` by construction: `ListLabRuntimeContainers` emits one entry per topology node state with no `InternalNode`/`ToolType` labels, so removing the filter from `PrintContainerInspect` does not regress the c9s inspect output.
- **No vanishing-node path for missing CPM slots**: `deployFabric` calls `cpmSlot()`, which errors when a distributed SR-SIM node defines neither slot A nor B, so a lab cannot reach a state where inspect would silently drop its only entry.
- **Component naming consistency**: `renameDone` is only set after `deployFabric` completes; `calcComponentName` always yields `<root>-<slot>` at container-creation time, which is exactly the convention `logicalNodeContainers` relies on.

### Test/CI verification (by inspection only, not executed)

- `Run Checked Pipeline` moved to `tests/common.robot` with `RETURN` of rc/stdout; `09-srsim-pause-container.robot` imports `../common.robot`, so the keyword resolves.
- `Deploy SR-SIM Lab`, `Destroy SR-SIM Lab`, and `Check SR-SIM License` exist in `tests/srsim.robot` and match the new `15-inspect-views` usage.
- The `.github/workflows/srlinux-tests.yml` matrix addition `05*.robot` matches only the new `tests/02-basic-srl/05-inspect-views.robot`; the srsim components shard addition matches the new `15-inspect-views.robot`.
- Expected values in both new suites trace correctly to the implementation: the deploy summary lists one entry per node (`linux srl`, `linux sr-a`) because `GetContainers` returns CPM A (or the holder fallback) per node; `--containers` views include holders and components; `-t` views exclude tools and internal containers.

### Coverage Notes

- All 15 changed paths and their callers were inspected. Verification was static: no tests, builds, or benchmarks were run, so runtime behavior claims (docker/podman/c9s) rest on code reading alone.
- No schema-domain change was introduced (no `clab.schema.json` properties added or removed), so no schema comparison was required.
- One residual observation deliberately not raised as a finding: the O(n²) `Contains`-based dedup in the `-t` merge is bounded by per-lab container counts (typically well under 100) and reuses existing runtime list helpers, so it does not warrant a change under the repository's performance ceilings.
